SMC_S13 premise corrected: the order's 'exploit the 85% generic fill rate' is backwards -- E004 (same FVG-fill construct) already established 85% as baseline (OBSERVED_NOT_DISTINCTIVE) and E004's own gaps fill LESS often than that baseline (71.48%, z~8.75). Reformulates SMC_S13 as an execution-economics hypothesis only (does NOT claim above-baseline fill rates), fixing two technical problems: next-open market entry (not a CE-50 limit order, eliminating M15 fill-ambiguity, consistent with every other Open-R family) and reconfirming the 20-bar Group-A horizon (the implemented 12 bars was an error applying Group B's rule to a point-event family). Notes SMC_S10's concept-reloop (Research Lab: 'BOS-as-displacement decouples magnitude from structure') as acknowledged, explicitly deferred.

Mandate: add CAND-0006 (weekly PWH/PWL, reformulated as Route 3 with no bias filter and direction taken from level kind) to the protocol batch after adversarial review returned SURVIVED with the observation that the reformulation MOVES the problem rather than removing it -- the collapse from 275 touches to 6 is genuinely eliminated, but the underlying anti-correlation is a family-level property and relocates into the fade direction, where the direction assumption now carries the entire bet. Five elements were requested; verification of the queue and the screening file first produced TWO corrections of record. First, the population figure: 275 is the Statistician own v2.7.40 measurement and is now propagating through the queue and the review verdict, but it counts ALL weekly levels while the policy trades COMPLETE weeks only. Measured separately: 538 COMPLETE levels yielding 258 touches, 34 PARTIAL yielding 17. The testable population is 258, not 275 -- a 6.2% correction to a number already circulating as an input. Second, the premise that session screening was still running: the results file already contains CAND-0001 through 0031 complete, including all six session candidates; what is missing is exactly what is new in the script, namely CAND-0006 and the five Primitive-B candidates. The triage criterion is therefore applicable NOW and K is no longer unknown. On the period-length prediction: the v2.7.42 metric required the DAILY fraction computed in the same pass, and the Validation Engine produced session, persistent and weekly funnels but NOT a daily one, so the comparison could not be made as specified. The Statistician measured the missing point directly, using the same ratified detector and the same alignment definition: session 33.6% (1,811 of 5,396), daily 26.6% (356 of 1,341), weekly 2.2% (6 of 275). The 356 aligned daily reproduces the survey n=356 exactly, confirming the same population is being measured. The predicted ordering holds -- a third independent confirmation -- but the prediction is CORRECTED in form rather than merely confirmed: degradation is NOT gradual, since session to daily loses seven points while daily to weekly collapses twelvefold, so the anti-correlation is mild up to the daily scale and catastrophic at the weekly one. Recorded as a weakening of the Statistician own generalization. The more interesting finding is an invariant: geometric touch rates are 47.7%, 47.3% and 48.1% across the three scales -- a range of 0.8 points across a period ratio of roughly thirty-five -- so the entire effect lives in the ALIGNMENT stage and the alternative explanation that long-period levels are simply too far away to be reached is excluded. On the direction test, the requirement transfers from the session-midpoint candidate but the CONSTRUCTION does not, for a structural reason: at a midpoint both arms have a target (the two session extremes), but at a weekly HIGH the fade arm has a target (the weekly LOW) while the inverse arm has none, because no weekly level exists ABOVE the weekly high. Keeping the target would make the arms differ in EXIT MECHANISM as well as direction, so any difference could not be attributed to direction. The specified matched pair therefore shares the entry, shares the risk distance (the fade arm own declared stop distance, floored), mirrors the stop, and exits BOTH arms on the week-boundary time-stop only -- the only symmetric option inventing no parameter. Non-degeneracy is verified rather than assumed: the stop breaks the mirror symmetry, which is precisely where a direction advantage would appear. The review amplifier is quantified: at weekly scale only 2.2% of touches have the market own bias on the fade side, so the policy is counter-bias in 97.8% of cases by construction (73.5% daily, 66.4% session), which makes the two arms ASYMMETRICALLY informative -- a fade win is strong because it beats an arm that is trend-aligned almost always, whereas an inverse win is confounded with plain trend-following and must additionally beat a bias-matched null on bars with no level. All four outcomes are pre-committed, the critical guard being that a significant inverse result does NOT promote the continuation thesis: that is a NEW hypothesis chosen AFTER seeing the result, requiring its own family slot and untouched data. Without that guard every outcome would be explicable and the test would be unfalsifiable. The decision rule is conjunctive: the policy must beat zero AND fade must beat inverse. On the COMPLETE-only conditioning, the review is directionally right and quantitatively wrong: PARTIAL levels are touched at 50.0% versus 48.0% for COMPLETE -- two points, in the predicted direction -- and constitute 5.9% of levels and 6.2% of touches, so the conditioning is declared WITH the figure rather than as an open-ended warning. On the offered FDR sub-family grouping the three level-fade candidates, the answer is NO, on derived grounds: a sub-family of three would apply alpha over 3 rather than over 7+K, LOOSENING the correction precisely for the three most favoured candidates -- the same per-batch selection trap already refused when the cumulative family was fixed. The observation is re-homed rather than discarded, to dependence (shared grammar means positive dependence, PRDS-compatible, BH stays valid) and to analysis (the three are the period gradient itself), mirroring the family/exploration ledger separation. On the stop threshold, the floor applies verbatim but with three properties not inherited from siblings: unlike the FVG-CE50 case the floor does NOT destroy the stop structural meaning, since a stop beyond the level remains beyond the level when widened; the target sits a full weekly range away so R:R survives flooring, meaning the floor bites on frequency rather than quality; and because the risk distance is SHARED across arms the floor applies identically to both and cannot tilt the direction comparison. On subset status, confirmed not a subset -- but measured NOT independent either: 40.7% of weekly touches fall on bars that are also daily level touches, and in 100% of those the implied fade direction AGREES while 0% oppose, so the dependence is positive, PRDS holds, BH stays valid and no partition is needed. This clarifies the earlier partition case retroactively: subset status was never the criterion there either -- the SIGN was. Finally, the triage criterion was applied to everything screened, with an uncomfortable result reported rather than buried: CAND-0003 and CAND-0010 satisfy ARCHIVE-NEGATIVE (zero positive years, zero positive regimes, n above 5,800 each), and CAND-0003 is one of the four authorized DEMO pilots with criteria the Statistician itself defined. The family is declared MONOTONE -- a candidate admitted to the family never leaves it, since removal would LOOSEN the threshold for the others, which is the same trap refused elsewhere in this mandate -- so the family stays at least 7 and post-admission archiving returns no slot. The DEMO decision is routed to the CEO, not taken. Family is now 16 (7 locked plus nine new category-C candidates), rising to at most 22 if the six unscreened ones all qualify, with exploration at 36. A misconception in the framing is corrected: alpha/m is the BH threshold only for the smallest p-value, the k-th ordered threshold being k*alpha/m, so at m=16 the fifth-ranked hypothesis faces 0.0156 rather than 0.0031 -- family growth costs far less than Bonferroni intuition suggests, which dissolves part of the anxiety driving the archive-to-preserve-power instinct. The Statistician own backlog is declared explicitly: three newly-qualified category-C candidates (0012, 0017, 0019) have cleared review and screening without a protocol, and that is the Statistician own arrears rather than anyone else, including 0017, the very case cited three times as a volume warning, which the criterion sends to formal test because its sign is mixed, applied as fixed even where the outcome is unwelcome.

Mandate: protocols for twelve candidates that cleared Red Team without one -- six MK structure candidates (CAND-0020 to 0025, all already screened and all negative) and six session candidates (CAND-0026 to 0031, screening still running) -- together with the question of whether already-screened negatives deserve formal protocols at all, given that every formally tested candidate widens the family and tightens the threshold for everyone including the ones that matter. Verified the screening file directly rather than accepting the summary, and found the six MK candidates are NOT a uniform group: the cited figure for CAND-0020 confirms exactly (34,006 trades, minus 15,408.7 R), but CAND-0023 has n=7 -- four times BELOW the reporting floor -- so it is not decisively negative but simply untested, since minus 1.9 R over seven trades is noise. Archiving it as negative would be a category error, absence of evidence not being evidence of absence, and its policy is a CONJUNCTION of two conditions, which produces small populations by construction -- the same shape as the weekly-levels case at n=6, where the degeneracy proved to be the framing rather than the mechanism. It therefore warrants a funnel decomposition rather than archival. Accordingly the triage criterion has THREE outcomes rather than two: ARCHIVE-NEGATIVE where n is adequate and expectancy is negative in every regime with no positive year, since a genuine edge degraded by cost or execution would show at least one positive subperiod and uniform negativity means the sign is structural; ARCHIVE-INSUFFICIENT where n falls below the floor, meaning the candidate was never testable and this is not negative evidence; and FORMAL PROTOCOL for anything mixed-sign or marginal. Applied, five go to archive-negative, CAND-0023 to archive-insufficient, and none to formal protocol. Adds an unrequested robustness check: whether archiving survives the one known pending revision, the realized-cost correction. At roughly 0.075 R per trade of maximum benefit, all five remain clearly negative, and the two closest to zero are NAMED NOW as the first to revisit should that correction land materially larger -- named in advance so that any later revisit cannot be a convenience choice. States that ARCHIVED is not REJECTED, since none was formally tested and therefore none is disproven; the correct label is that it does not warrant a family slot on current evidence, and a candidate may return if evidence changes, consuming a slot at that point rather than passing through a free door. On family governance, separates two ledgers that are easily conflated: the FAMILY ledger, counting hypotheses formally tested, which sets alpha; and the EXPLORATION ledger, counting candidates looked at, which exists for honest reporting. Archiving negatives cannot inflate the false-discovery rate, because that rate governs the fraction of REJECTIONS that are false and an untested or decisively-negative candidate produces no rejection at all -- this is not a loophole but a consequence of what the correction actually measures. What silent archiving WOULD bias is the apparent hit rate, which is precisely why the exploration count must remain visible even though it never enters alpha. That resolves the mandate's tension without forcing a choice between destroying power by testing everything and hiding exploration by archiving quietly. Family is therefore 7 plus K, with K fixed by the pre-declared criterion before the session screening completes, so it cannot be adjusted on results. Verifies that the subset relations among the session candidates are POSITIVE dependence and PRDS-compatible, so BH remains valid, unlike the single negative-dependence pair already resolved by partition. Specifies the session-batch protocols: the incremental-value null on identical bars for the four subset candidates; and for CAND-0028 the observation that its declared approach-side rule is a load-bearing assumption carrying the entire trade direction, so its null is not zero but the REVERSED rule on the same touch bars -- otherwise a positive result could stem entirely from midpoint touches having an edge in some direction while the rule itself contributes nothing. The feed-alignment warning is routed as a DEMO-stage precondition rather than a protocol element, being a backtest-to-live transfer gap of the same category as cost being observed rather than modeled. Records that the Statistician's own earlier alarm about the widened F4 surface was MEASURED at zero dual-sign bars across all three regimes, so the flag was correct as a precaution but the risk is empirically nil, making the collision rule on CAND-0022 inert though costless to retain. Finally, fixes the confirmation metric for the earlier period-length prediction BEFORE the session numbers arrive, including the explicit refutation condition, so that a disconfirmation of the Statistician's own prediction would be reported as plainly as a confirmation.

Mandate: specify the density filter Red Team required (RT-CODE-A-0004) before any candidate may be built on primitive B, the persistent session levels -- the class Alpha had held aside precisely because no such filter existed. Derives the filter's FORM before touching any data, on the observation that Red Team's verdict contains TWO distinct charges needing different remedies: density (89 to 188 levels active simultaneously) and unfalsifiability by saturation (price is always near some level, so 'price reacts to a level' has no content). A RANK filter -- nearest-N or most-recent-N -- fixes the first and makes the second WORSE, because it always returns N levels, so price remains near a level by construction and saturation is merely hidden at a fixed count rather than removed. Only a THRESHOLD filter can return the EMPTY SET, and the empty set is exactly what falsifiability requires. Age was rejected as the primary axis for a separate reason: a short age bound collapses B into A, since persistence is B's entire premise, while a long one bounds nothing -- whereas distance preserves the premise, an old distant level being irrelevant now yet eligible again if price returns to it. The filter was fixed BEFORE measuring: a level is eligible at bar j if and only if the absolute distance from its price to close[j-1] is at most k times ATR14[j-1], with k=1.0 primary and 0.5 and 2.0 pre-declared as sensitivities. k=1.0 is not invented for the occasion but is the lab's own risk unit, the stop distance used throughout the DEMO line, so an eligible level sits within one unit of risk of price. No-lookahead is demonstrated rather than asserted: the filter reads only close[j-1] and ATR14[j-1], both complete before bar j opens, plus the primitive's own availability constraint -- and the one-bar lag is deliberate, since using the current bar's close would consult the very bar being evaluated and would not be executable live. The effectiveness threshold is derived from the already-published baseline rather than invented: median at most 9 and maximum at most 19, an order of magnitude below the measured 89 and 188, plus a non-zero zero-eligible fraction as the falsifiability condition, that last one carrying an interpretive rule rather than an invented numeric cutoff. The result was MEASURED, not estimated, across all 130,491 discovery bars, with the unfiltered baseline reproducing Red Team's 89 and 188 exactly, confirming the same object is being filtered rather than a different one. At k=1.0 the median active count falls to 0 and the maximum to 6, a thirty-one-fold reduction at the extreme -- so the pre-declared PRIMARY passed and no re-selection occurred after the numbers were seen. Falsifiability is quantified directly: unfiltered, 0.0% of bars have zero eligible levels, meaning price is literally always near a level and confirming Red Team's charge numerically; at k=1.0 that figure is 83.6%, so on five bars in six there is no level in play at all and the claim can finally fail. A second measurement establishes that the filter does not destroy the event population: 53.3% of touches survive despite the thirty-one-fold density cut, which is structural rather than fortunate, since a level about to be touched is by construction already near price and therefore passes the filter exactly when it matters, while what gets removed is the distant levels that were never going to be touched -- which is the dilution itself. States plainly what the filter does NOT fix: the 8,833 retained touches are the same order of magnitude as the three cited failures (18,275 trades at minus 2,432 dollars; 34,006 at minus 15,409 R; 18,852 at minus 2,605 R), so the filter resolves saturation and falsifiability as demanded but NOT volume, leaving any candidate on B still exposed to the too-many-zones pattern and required to add its own selectivity and report its final trigger count BEFORE any performance figure. Both prohibitions are honoured explicitly: the filter compensates nothing, leaving D2, D7, F4 and the block-boundary conventions untouched; and the threshold was not chosen after results, with the decisive safeguard that the density measurement is P&L-BLIND, containing only level and touch counts and therefore incapable of serving as a backdoor for tuning on outcomes.

Mandate: specify three reaction detectors to unblock CAND-0004 (liquidity void), CAND-0005 (BPR) and CAND-0006 (weekly levels), which have Part A and Part B written but are NOT_CURRENTLY_TESTABLE for want of a TRIGGER rather than a stop. All three are specified by mirroring already-ratified conventions rather than inventing parallels, following the session_levels.py precedent. The decisive contribution concerns CAND-0006. Asked to say BEFORE construction whether a weekly touch detector could produce a usable population, the Statistician MEASURED it rather than estimating -- a temporary uncommitted script, deleted after use, reusing only ratified primitives and the existing survey's own load path. The funnel decomposes cleanly across the three discovery regimes: 572 weekly levels emitted (538 COMPLETE), 275 of them touched geometrically (48.1%, entirely healthy), but only 6 also bias-aligned (2.2% of those touched) -- which reproduces the survey's n=6 and its 3/2/1 regime split exactly, confirming it is the same population being decomposed rather than a different one. The collapse therefore sits entirely at the bias stage, and its cause is structural rather than statistical: a weekly high can only be touched by price rallying up to reach it, yet its trade direction is short, requiring both higher-timeframe biases to be down -- the two conditions contradict each other by construction, since reaching a weekly extreme essentially means the trend on comparable horizons is running the other way. The raw counts confirm the mechanism directly: highs were touched 147 times but aligned only twice; lows touched 128 times but aligned only four times. Generalizes this with a testable prediction: for ANY prior-period extreme, being touched and being bias-aligned-for-reversal are structurally anti-correlated, and the anti-correlation worsens as the period lengthens (daily weak at n=356, weekly severe at n=6), so sub-daily session levels should suffer LESS than daily ones -- cheap to verify at the first session-levels measurement. The operational conclusion saves the requested round, but differently than anticipated: BUILD the weekly detector, since it works and yields 275 usable events, but RE-FRAME CAND-0006 rather than merely unblocking it, because the degeneracy was never the detector's fault. Three re-framings are offered (bias supplying direction rather than eligibility, an inverted continuation thesis, or no bias at all), none chosen since that is Alpha's decision. The common diagnosis that a missing detector blocked CAND-0006 was simply wrong. On void reactions: mirrors the ratified FVG three-tier reaction gradient, since a void is the same class of object (a skipped price interval) -- partial fill at the midpoint, complete fill on traversal, and rejection reusing the D6 wick-sweep-reject signature verbatim rather than inventing a fourth rejection convention -- with zone and polarity taken from the earlier v2.7.27 derivation, D7 first-occurrence recording per event, and the anti-E010 selection/measurement window separation preserved. On BPR reactions: confirms that direction comes from bias and that the detector must not encode it, but identifies that 'complete fill' and 'rejection' require a SIDE to be meaningful at all, and resolves this by having the detector emit direction-agnostic geometry INCLUDING the entry side, so that a policy can combine entry side with bias and must declare that rule explicitly -- the same treatment Mid received in the session-levels specification. On weekly touches: mirrors detect_level_touches verbatim with the week window replacing the day window, using EXCEEDANCE rather than containment because these are genuine period extremes where liquidity rests, which is the already-settled High/Low versus Mid distinction and answers the question without requiring a new decision. On the PARTIAL flag for quarantined weeks: the detector emits both and propagates completeness, with exclusion left as a declared policy choice rather than a hidden filter -- but requires COMPLETE and PARTIAL be reported SEPARATELY on a derived ground, since a PARTIAL week's extremes are computed over fewer days and are therefore systematically less extreme, hence closer to price and touched more often, so pooling them would inflate the measured touch rate (measured split: 538 COMPLETE, 34 PARTIAL).

Mandate (two tasks): the CEO's RATIFICATION of MK-01 market_structure.py and MK-02 liquidity_mechanics.py, recorded with three non-blocking open items attached; and a mechanical specification for session levels. On the ratification: verified VE's cascade measurement directly rather than accepting it -- 40.9% of break-bars carried two or more breaks, a maximum of 24 on a single bar, and 542 breaks lost forever under the old semantics, all exact. Added an internal consistency check of the Statistician's own: breaks_new minus breaks_old equals 542, matching the independently-derived refs-lost-forever count to the unit, which empirically CONFIRMS the prediction derived at v2.7.38 that the suppressing elif was DROPPING breaks rather than merely delaying them, and that the entire count increase is exactly the previously-lost set rather than inflation of another kind. Sharpens one point rather than restating it: VE's conclusion that zero of four consumer sites change their reference swing is correct, but the kind-filter argument alone does not establish it, since two breaks of the SAME kind can now share one bar and the strict index comparison in _first_break_after cannot separate them, leaving list order to decide. The operative reason is the tie behaviour, and that holds precisely BECAUSE of the descending-order rule specified at v2.7.38 to preserve behaviour -- so the ordering rule is recorded as LOAD-BEARING rather than incidental, since changing it would silently change the reference in four strategy sites, and it is frozen as an invariant with a dedicated test. Open item one, F4: specifies that simultaneous opposite change-of-character readings are NOT a detector defect but a faithful report of a genuinely contradictory labelled structure, so suppressing either side inside the detector would hide real ambiguity and reintroduce the exact class of artifact just eliminated; both are emitted, and the downstream interpretation rule is fail-closed by default (no signal on a contradictory bar), consistent with this lab's established fail-closed convention, with any alternative required to be declared and pre-registered rather than defaulted silently in code -- plus a requirement that F4 frequency be measured in the same pass so that calling it non-blocking becomes a fact rather than an assumption. Open item two: specifies the four missing tests as acceptance criteria and identifies which two carry the most weight -- the reference-selection test, which converts the ordering rule from a convention into an enforced invariant so that any future reordering breaks a test instead of silently changing strategy semantics, and the aggregate-conservation test, which is precisely the invariant the old defect violated and that no existing suite checked. Open item three: accepts VE's causal finding that the SET of breaks changes rather than the reference, confirms the re-run remains an execution correction that does NOT consume family (the hypothesis is unchanged; the detector under-delivered events the hypothesis always covered, making this the first correct run rather than a second attempt), and specifies the pre-commitment that keeps that true -- exact scope of S2, S3 and S11 only with S10 excluded and S1, S7, S13, S16, S17 verified untouched, identical metrics and regimes and cost and floor, the new result replacing the old in EITHER direction including a worse one, mandatory reporting of old versus new counts so the population change is visible rather than buried in an average, and no other parameter permitted to change alongside. On session levels: specifies three levels per closed session instance (High, Low, and the geometric Mid) plus a touch detector, mirroring the ratified PDH/PDL conventions bar for bar -- availability at the first bar of the next instance per Q4, the D3_bis reset on a block's first instance, and D7 consumption -- and reusing the existing runs helper for segmentation rather than introducing new code. Decides the primitive itself is GENERAL, with every closed instance emitting levels tagged by source session, while the restriction to any particular pairing belongs to policy, grounded in the ratified Module-7 precedent that a generic locator must not carry a hypothesis choice; the classic Asia-to-London case remains fully expressible as a declared policy filter where it is auditable. Flags that the session clock (UTC hours) and the day anchor (17:00 New York) do not align, so a late-session run can straddle a day boundary, and declines to cut on days since nothing requires it and it would fragment instances -- while requiring the straddle frequency and the instance-length distribution be measured rather than assumed, since block-truncated instances can be a single bar and yield degenerate levels. Specifies the two lifetime variants as genuinely DISTINCT primitives as requested, and attaches a concrete control to the accumulating variant derived from an already-paid failure: the demand-zone-by-gap case reached 18,275 trades and a $2,432 loss before anyone noticed, so active-level count and total touch count must be measured as a standalone diagnostic BEFORE any candidate is built on it. Adds a structural distinction that would otherwise have been a silent gap: Mid is not the same class of object as High and Low, since the latter are liquidity levels with stops resting beyond them while Mid is a geometric midpoint with no such interpretation -- so Mid requires its own containment-based touch test, has NO intrinsic side meaning direction cannot come from the level and must be declared by any policy using it, and all three must be reported separately rather than pooled.

Mandate: the cascade-break timing semantics for MK-01's detect_breaks, decided by the CEO after Red Team's RT-CODE-A-0002 finding that stacked swings have their breaks recorded one per bar, so the oldest of N stacked swings breaks N-1 bars late. Specifies the corrected semantics mechanically: every swing exceeded by the close of bar c produces its break AT bar c, each still consumed exactly once (D7 unchanged) under unchanged strict inequalities (D2 unchanged). Identifies TWO independent staggering vectors where the finding named one: the single-slot live_* pointers, which mean only the most recent swing of each label is ever evaluated at all, AND the within-direction if/elif, which suppresses an exceeded lower-high whenever a higher-high breaks on the same bar. The mandate's own two-stacked-higher-highs example illustrates only the first; the decision as WORDED ('all swings exceeded by the close of bar c') covers both, and is implemented as worded -- while explicitly flagging the consequence the example does not show, namely that a structure break and a change-of-character can now co-occur on one bar against distinct reference swings, which is not double-counting but exactly what 'one break per distinct swing' requires, named as a conscious change to a long-standing precedence rather than left as a silent side effect. Corrects the framing that the count is strictly conserved: the suppressing elif did not merely delay a break, it could DROP one permanently if the condition lapsed on the following bar, so the new semantics yields MORE breaks in that case -- not a change to D7 but the delivery of what D7 already specified and the one-break-per-bar artifact under-delivered. On intra-bar ordering, answers the question with a concrete existing consumer rather than in the abstract: trading_strategies.py's _first_break_after selects with a strict index comparison that cannot separate breaks now sharing the same bar index, so list order becomes semantically load-bearing exactly where ties never previously arose. Specifies descending order by the reference swing's index, chosen on behaviour-preserving grounds rather than aesthetics -- the current code's live pointer holds the most recent swing, so most-recent-first keeps existing consumers on the same reference swing and confines the change to timing alone, whereas ascending would have silently changed the reference as well; the index is unique per swing (verified: at most one swing is emitted per bar), so the order is total with no tie-break needed. Flags that the semantic question underneath -- whether 'the level broken' should mean the nearest or the furthest of several broken on one bar -- belongs to the owner of trading_strategies.py and must be confirmed deliberately rather than inherited from an ordering default. Notes that F4 (simultaneous opposite change-of-character on one bar) is NOT resolved here and that its surface area GROWS, since each direction can now emit several breaks per bar. Most consequentially, corrects the mandate's own premise after verifying it directly rather than accepting it: the candidate policies are genuinely clean, since institutional_levels and imbalance_mechanics import only the inert Block dataclass, but trading_strategies.py DOES call detect_breaks at four sites (detect_s2, detect_s3, detect_s10, detect_s11), and that consumption is timing-sensitive because _first_break_after filters on a twenty-bar qualification window anchored to the break index -- so a mis-timed break can move a setup into or out of ELIGIBILITY, not merely shift its entry bar. The already-measured descriptive results for S2, S3 and S11 are therefore affected in principle. Verified that detect_s1 does not call it, so the SMC_S1 statistical rejection stands untouched, as do S7, S13, S16 and S17. Calibrates this honestly rather than overstating: the cascade case is reachable but was never exercised by any test, so its frequency is unknown -- requires VE to measure that frequency alongside implementation and only then decide whether a re-run is warranted, noting that such a re-run would be an execution correction on the same hypothesis and therefore NOT family-consuming. Triggers no re-run, but states that 'nothing re-runs' cannot be asserted before that measurement exists.

Mandate: the first realized transaction cost measured on a real DEMO account (one round-trip, both legs filled at the requested price, zero slippage, observed spread $0.05 against the model's $0.20) and what would be required before any verdict could be reopened on it. NOTHING is reopened here -- one observation establishes nothing, agreed without qualification. Verified the constant's provenance at source rather than accepting the framing: cost_round_trip=0.20 is not a measurement at all but a construction, 2*(spread_ticks+slip_ticks)*TICK, in which spread_ticks=5 came from a stated range and slip_ticks=5 came from an explicit CONVENTION that slippage equals spread -- never observed. That decomposition reframes the whole question: the 4x gap is not one error but TWO, with very different evidential standing. The spread half (modeled 0.10 versus observed 0.05, roughly 2x over) is passively measurable and the observation bears on it directly. The slippage half (modeled 0.10 versus observed 0.00) has no empirical basis whatsoever and CANNOT be measured by observing spread at all, because slippage materialises at size, on volatile bars and on gaps -- precisely the conditions in which every one of these strategies triggers. A single calm, minimum-size fill showing zero slippage therefore says almost nothing about the slippage these strategies would actually pay. Notes as a consistency check that the observed 5 ticks sits at the LOW end of the 5-15 tick range originally stated, exactly what a calm-moment sample would look like, which frames rather than undermines it. Flags for verification at source that a $0.05 gold spread implies a raw/ECN account, which typically charges commission separately -- if so the cited figure is not the full round-trip cost, the same discipline applied when the tick size itself was verified. On sampling: the estimand is not the mean spread but the mean cost CONDITIONAL ON A TRADE TRIGGERING, since cost enters expectancy linearly but trades do not occur at random moments -- they cluster on volatility events where spreads widen, so fixed-interval calendar sampling is systematically biased LOW. Continuous collection remains the right raw mechanism, but the estimate must be reweighted to the trigger distribution, which is only possible if stratification labels are recorded alongside. The strata reuse already-ratified primitives (four sessions crossed with three volatility states). The decisive technical point: 30-second observations are massively autocorrelated, so effective sample size is measured in DAYS, not ticks -- clustering on day-by-session using the block-bootstrap machinery already ratified in this lab, with the standing minimum of 25 applied to distinct days per cell rather than raw observations, which honestly implies weeks-to-months of collection rather than hours. The stopping rule is derived rather than an invented precision target: the entire 95% interval must fall below the modeled constant. On which verdicts could reopen: corrects the stated reason for non-recomputability, since edge_brut was verified at v2.7.24 to equal expectancy plus exactly 0.20, meaning it reconstructs raw gross and is arithmetically cost-independent -- the real obstacle is populational, because cost sets both the ATR eligibility floor and the minimum executable risk, which jointly determine WHICH trades enter the sample at all, a non-additive channel that genuinely forbids paper recomputation. Applies the Statistician's own earlier standard to this new evidence: an ATR-rescaling inference was rejected at v2.7.25 partly as out-of-domain extrapolation from today's market onto historical data, and a present-day cost measurement is the same category of inference in the favorable direction -- rejecting it when unfavorable and accepting it when favorable would be a double standard, so a current measurement establishes CURRENT cost and does not by itself reopen any historical backtest verdict, while acknowledging the genuine asymmetry that a mechanical constant is stronger evidence than a behavioral edge. Sorts verdicts by decisive reason rather than outcome: the OBDZ rejection IS cost-sensitive, since gross was positive in every regime and cost consumed it, and its deliberately scoped label already anticipated revisability; the SMC_S1 statistical rejection does NOT reopen, because it rested on gross edge being near-zero with inconsistent sign across regimes and a lower cost cannot manufacture an edge that was never reliably positive; and the zone-versus-pullback excursion signal is untouched in both directions, having never involved cost at any point. Sets three cumulative reopening conditions rather than one, and leaves the constant-versus-variable question empirical with the discriminating analysis (spread-to-volatility elasticity) specified in advance -- explicitly placing the Statistician's own v2.7.24 structural explanation of the OBDZ failure at risk, since an elasticity near one would refute it. Specifies collection fields for passive observation while stating plainly that passive observation can only ever correct the spread half, and requires real-fill capture for the slippage and commission halves. States that a re-run under corrected cost is a NEW test consuming family, not a free reopening -- otherwise a corrected cost becomes an unlimited re-test door for everything that has failed.

Mandate: DEMO evaluation criteria for CAND-0002, CAND-0003 and CAND-0007, following Red Team's conditional Part-B survivals (RT-OPS-B-0002). Applies the already-ratified CAND-0001 gate verbatim to all three -- worst-case intrabar hierarchy STOP over TIME-STOP over TARGET with INVALID_EXECUTION kept narrow, the min_executable_risk floor with 1R sized on the floored distance and effective_spread taken as realized, and the forward-only target scan -- reused rather than re-derived, alongside the three deferrals resolved identically (min_trades=25 as a reporting-suppression floor and explicitly not a power floor since DEMO runs no test, regimes_permitted with no filter since regime is not computable live, and cost observed rather than modeled with mandatory reconciliation). Risk methods remain Alpha's and frozen; nothing here designs one. On CAND-0002, sharpens Red Team's Finding H rather than restating it: the block-boundary time-stop is not merely a potentially multi-week horizon, because a block is a discovery-data construct (the manifest's regime segments), so on a forward-running DEMO account there is no current block and no boundary to reach -- the third leg of the 'first of' rule never fires and the horizon degenerates to no time-stop whatsoever, unbounded by construction rather than by accident. This is the same category as the regimes_permitted ruling and the live-versus-retrospective distinction fixed earlier. The replacement term is explicitly NOT designed here and is routed to Alpha as a specification request for a forward-computable horizon. What is imposed instead is measurement only, with no invented threshold: holding duration bucketed onto the lab's own already-derived constants (the 20-bar Group A reaction horizon, the 92-bar empirical day, the 460-bar empirical week, and beyond), plus overnight and weekend crossings and peak concurrent exposure -- zero new constants, with any decision to cap left to Alpha and the CEO. On CAND-0003, the tightest gate, adds two consequences derived beyond what the review reported. First, because the stop IS the ratified Q4 inversion boundary, applying the floor pushes the stop beyond that boundary, so on small gaps the floor does not merely resize the position -- it destroys the stop's structural meaning, and the policy's own stated rationale ceases to hold for exactly those trades; flagged and routed, not repaired, since repairing it would be redesigning risk. Second, arithmetically: a midpoint entry makes stop and target distances equal (which is why R:R is approximately 1 as a geometric consequence rather than a choice), but the floor widens only the stop while the target remains fixed at the near edge, so floored trades exhibit systematically collapsing risk-reward, worst on the smallest gaps -- precisely the routine population the review flagged. Floored and unfloored trades must therefore be reported separately with realized R:R per group, since pooling would conceal a structurally disadvantaged subpopulation beneath a single mean. Third, reframes the S1-resolved fraction from an audit field into a validity indicator: because one ordinary bar routinely spans both edges of a small gap, a large share of outcomes would be determined by the worst-case tie-break convention rather than by observed market behaviour, so the unambiguously-resolved and convention-resolved fractions must be reported side by side, with the explicit interpretive rule that a convention-dominated result says little about the mechanism -- no numeric cutoff invented. On CAND-0007, notes that planned risk-reward is computable at entry since both the combined stop and the opposite-level target are known then, making it a declared per-trade field computed on the floored distance with the sub-1 fraction reported in aggregate; declines to impose a risk-reward filter because that would be a new entry condition and therefore Alpha's, and notes the symmetry with CAND-0003 (different causes, identical measurable consequence, same reporting format). Binds the review's observation that CAND-0007's Part B reuses CAND-0001's exit while its entry zone sits inside CAND-0003's, so the W-incr incremental test already specified must now cover the risk layer as well as entry -- otherwise apparent confluence value could arise entirely from the wider stop. Carries the CAND-0003 gate verbatim: if the floor and worst-case convention cannot be shown enforced, that policy does not trade. Reaffirms that DEMO is not statistical validation, consumes no family despite these three belonging to the family of 7 for future formal tests, and that no DEMO figure promotes anything. Also records that the CAND-0008/0009/0010 protocols requested as a separate item were already delivered in the prior mandate rather than redoing them.

Mandate: the CAND-0001 vs CAND-0009 partition decision flagged by Red Team as W-partition, plus statistical protocols for the RT-OPS-A-0002 batch (CAND-0008, CAND-0009, CAND-0010). The conflict: CAND-0001 trades the REJECTION off a prior-day level while CAND-0009 trades the BREAK of the same level, and on displacement-touch bars both fire in OPPOSITE directions -- with an asymmetric boundary, since CAND-0009 cleanly excludes the reversal case in its own no_trade_rules while CAND-0001 has no clause excluding breaks, so on every forceful break CAND-0001 systematically takes the losing side. DECISION: option 2 (disjoint test populations) as primary with option 3's measurement as a mandatory secondary, and explicitly NOT option 1 -- that being a policy modification belonging to Alpha, and one not even recommended yet, since CAND-0001 v2.0 is already frozen, already through the Part-B adversarial attack, and already carries published DEMO criteria, so changing the mechanism before any evidence justifies it would invalidate that entire chain. The reasoning separates two questions that were being conflated: scientifically, on a displacement-touch bar the reversal thesis (the level holds) is falsified by the very bar being measured, so those bars are a contaminated subpopulation rather than a neutral sample and the sharp test excludes them; operationally, the policy as written does trade them, so describing real behaviour requires including them. The DIFFERENCE between the two measurements is precisely the measured cost of the missing exclusion -- delivering option 3's substance as a byproduct of a clean test rather than instead of one, at zero additional data collection since it is the same events under two partitions. The honest weakness is declared rather than buried: tested population is not the traded population, which is exactly why the secondary measurement is mandatory rather than optional. Adds a technical finding of the Statistician's own that decides between the options on grounds stronger than preference: because the two candidates hold opposite positions on overlap bars, their test statistics are NEGATIVELY dependent in proportion to the overlap fraction, and BH-FDR -- the correction already fixed at v2.7.33 -- has a proven guarantee only under independence or positive regression dependence, not under negative dependence, which would instead require Benjamini-Yekutieli at roughly 2.59x severity across a family of 7, penalising five candidates with no involvement in the conflict. The disjoint construction eliminates the shared bars and thereby RESTORES the validity of the already-pre-registered correction, making it the only option that does not force a severe methodological downgrade. Notes for completeness that the subset relations elsewhere in the family (CAND-0010 within CAND-0003, CAND-0007 within both its constituents) are positive dependence and PRDS-compatible, so BH remains sound there. Flags a live consequence for already-published work: the CAND-0001 DEMO criteria at v2.7.34 predate this finding, so a DEMO account would systematically take the losing side on every forceful break -- adds a reporting requirement (the displacement-touch subset reported separately, with all results shown both with and without it) that measures the effect on the real account without modifying the policy, leaving the exclusion decision with Alpha and the CEO. Confirms W-incr on CAND-0010 as an identical pattern to CAND-0007: every stack trigger is a CE-50 reaction plus a density condition, a strict subset, so the null is incremental value over single-FVG restricted to the identical bars, never a random null. Resolves W-dir-mask as an implementation precision rather than routing it to Alpha, because the policy's own trigger prose and no_trade_rules already require direction alignment in two independent places and only the mask expression is loose -- implementing it aligned is fidelity to the policy, not a change to it. Updates the multiple-testing family from 4 to 7 cumulatively, correcting the Statistician's own earlier specification: all seven arise from the same continuous-production line over the same discovery data, and maintaining separate per-batch families would be precisely the selection trap the discipline exists to prevent. The update is free because no test has yet been EXECUTED, and is flagged as urgent because four candidates were unblocked to Validation Engine during the writing of this document, meaning the first run must start from the corrected threshold rather than be corrected afterward. Protocols specified for all three new candidates, all still blocked on unspecified Part B.

Mandate: DEMO evaluation criteria for CAND-0001 PDH-PDL v2.0 (DEMO_BASELINE), the single CEO-authorized pilot policy -- defines how the DEMO run is measured and what the execution engine must enforce, explicitly WITHOUT designing the risk method, which is Alpha's and frozen at commit 1558397. Verified all three safety-gate sources directly before writing rather than paraphrasing from memory: the frozen policy itself, Red Team's RT-OPS-B-0001 Part-B attack report, and docs/MIN_STOP_FLOOR_PREREG.md (exact formula plus the pre-registered constants k_spread=2, k_tick=5, k_atr=0.10). Corrects a direction error in Statistician's own first draft: the policy defers min_trades TO the Statistician (lines 50, 69, 93), not the reverse, and line 93 additionally defers regimes_permitted and the cost convention -- all three are fixed here rather than one. min_trades is set at 25 but the category is corrected: Alpha calls it a statistical-power floor and it cannot be one, since power is defined only against a test and DEMO deliberately runs none -- it is a reporting-suppression floor (suppress the figures, do not merely flag them), and reaching it confers no validity whatever. regimes_permitted is set to no filter, for a DEMO-specific reason rather than a general preference: regime is a retrospectively-derived label that is not computable live, exactly the live-versus-methodological distinction fixed at v2.7.30, so restricting a forward-running DEMO account by it could not be executed honestly -- it remains a reporting stratification only. The cost convention captures the central DEMO-versus-backtest distinction: on a DEMO account cost is OBSERVED, not modeled, so realized spread and slippage must be recorded per fill and reconciled explicitly against the lab's modeled constant -- with the further note that a systematic divergence would be information about every backtest this lab has produced, while explicitly declining to draw that conclusion here without its own separate verification. Also binds Gate 2's effective_spread term to the realized value, since on DEMO the true figure is actually available rather than assumed. Carries Red Team's gate condition verbatim: if the DEMO engine cannot be shown to enforce the three gates, the policy does not trade. Part-A controls (W-sel/W-conf/W-ovl/W-e010) are referenced to STAT-BATCH-A-0001 rather than restated. Handoff to Validation Engine for executability and mechanical gate verification.

Mandate: specification (not implementation, per explicit instruction) for two HTF probabilistic context descriptors -- a 4H regime calculator and a 1H bias calculator, both replacing an existing binary flag with a genuinely probabilistic empirical-frequency output. The 4H regime calculator defines exactly three mutually exclusive states -- Compression, Strong Trend, Range -- built entirely from primitives already frozen in market_state.py (the 460-bar rolling P10 Parkinson log-range compression test and the E010 displacement-plus-body expansion test), with a disclosed priority rule (compression wins) for the rare case both technically fire on the same bar simultaneously. Its probability figure is not classification confidence (compression/expansion are already deterministic once a bar closes) but an empirical forward-persistence frequency -- does the same state still hold some number of bars later -- with that horizon derived, not chosen freely, from the already-established 92-M15-bar empirical daily median (v2.5.5/v2.7.13), converted to roughly six H4 bars. The 1H bias calculator keeps the existing two-state binary (ema20 above or below ema50) unchanged and converts it to [P_LONG, P_SHORT] via an order-1 conditional/transition frequency -- conditioning only on the immediately current state rather than a longer history, an explicit choice for cell-count robustness with only two states -- reported across a 4-12 hour horizon window (8h primary, 4h/12h as sensitivity) rather than collapsed to one arbitrary point. Both calculators share a single estimation/application window split that reuses the already-established discovery regime boundaries rather than inventing a percentage: bear+bull for estimation (roughly 80% of discovery, chronologically first), correction for application (roughly 20%, and the regime closest in time to the real, untouched holdout, making it the most meaningful available generalization check) -- explicitly not touching holdout itself. States a critical distinction clearly: regime is a one-time methodological split device used only to validate the calibration, never a live conditioning input in either formula, since which historical regime the market is 'in' is not something computable going forward -- unlike session, which is genuinely live-computable but is left as an explicitly flagged, open (not silently added) extension for the 1H calculator specifically, since H1 bars align cleanly with session boundaries while H4 bars straddle them. Confirms neither calculator consumes family -- an even cleaner case than the recent execution-characterization survey, since these touch no net_R, no P&L, no trade outcome at all, purely market-state persistence frequencies. States explicitly that any future compound trigger using either descriptor as an entry filter requires its own separate pre-registration and family accounting -- the descriptors themselves are free to use as context, their incorporation into an actual tradeable construction is not. Reuses the N_MIN=25 suppress-not-flag small-cell rule from the prior mandate unchanged. Authorizes nothing beyond the specification itself -- no implementation, no run.

Mandate: zone-type execution-characterization spec for the ten new zone types -- confirms non-consumption of family, specifies the small-cell rule, authorizes the wave-gated run. Confirms that running the ten new zone types through the full OBDZ-002 execution contract (SL=1.0x/TP1=2.0x/TP2=3.0x/floor=0.60x ATR14[t], entry=t+1 no confirmation, horizon=min(entry+20,EOD), 75/25 partial exit with breakeven -- identical, unmodified, to OBDZ-002 itself) rather than the plain MFE/MAE comparison still does NOT consume family: the distinction this project has used throughout is the presence of a WP-5' p-value and a formal accept/reject verdict, not how detailed the descriptive output is. No p-value is computed here; any positive-looking cell remains a candidate requiring separate, family-consuming pre-registration -- the exact mechanism that already protects the MFE/MAE survey from becoming a backdoor multiple-testing exercise. Flags explicitly, not merely formally, an elevated risk specific to this survey: because it reports winrate/expectancy/edge in the same units and shape as a genuine backtest result (unlike the more abstract MFE/MAE figures), and produces roughly 220 cells across the ten types (aggregate+3 regimes+4 sessions+12 regime-by-session+2 polarities per type), the temptation to treat a good-looking cell as already-validated is real and must be actively resisted -- insists no cell's descriptive statistics may be cited as evidence of a real edge without the full, separate pre-registration process. Specifies the small-cell rule precisely, adding one important completion beyond simply labeling: below n=25, the descriptive statistics (winrate, expectancy in R and dollars, gross edge, net total, concentration figures, TP1-to-TP2 conversion) are SUPPRESSED entirely, not merely flagged as unreliable -- a small-sample winrate or expectancy figure looks visually identical to a real one regardless of any accompanying caveat, so only n and the INSUFFICIENT_N marker are reported. Flags two additions (an aggregate cell and polarity stratification) not mentioned in the order but established as mandatory throughout this entire track without exception -- added explicitly and transparently, not silently, inviting correction if not wanted. Reaffirms family=12 unchanged (the count of surveyed zone types, independent of how detailed each survey happens to be) and authorizes the wave-gated execution run (same wave ordering as the descriptive survey), reusing the identical trigger population already established for the MFE/MAE characterization rather than recomputing independently.

Mandate: ATR-rescaling-to-current-volatility inference REJECTED, not a valid family-3 justification. CTO proposed reinterpreting the OBDZ-002 rejection as a rejection of the TEST PERIOD rather than the strategy: cost is fixed at $0.20 while gross edge scales with each survivor's own ATR (confirmed at v2.7.24), and today's gold ATR (~7.40) is 3.4x-5.8x the discovery-era regime medians (1.27-2.19) -- rescaling the historical edge_brut figures by that same ratio puts all three regimes comfortably above cost. Verified the underlying mechanism directly in partial_exit.py (R=abs(entry_price-sl_price), net_R=LEG1_FRAC*(r1-cost/R)+LEG2_FRAC*(r2-cost/R), cost=0.20 fixed) -- confirms cost's drag genuinely shrinks in R-terms as R (ATR-proportional) grows; this part of the reasoning is mechanically correct, not disputed. Rejects the inference itself on three independent grounds. First: H0 was never rejected in any regime (v2.7.24) -- rescaling an unproven point estimate by an ATR ratio produces the same unproven number, algebraically inflated, not new evidence of a real edge; if the true population edge is zero or negative, no scaling factor turns it positive, only larger in dollar terms. Second: the three discovery regimes already refute the portability this argument silently assumes -- bull's R-multiple edge (-0.0776) is far more negative than bear's (-0.0134) despite bull having the LOWEST ATR of the three, meaning R-edge is driven by regime-specific conditions, not by ATR level itself, so there is no single stable R-edge value to transplant onto an unobserved present-day regime. Third: the calculation extrapolates 3.4x-5.8x beyond the entire ATR range ever observed in the fitted data, onto a market that has structurally evolved for a decade-plus, while additionally assuming transaction cost stays flat at $0.20 despite a 3-6x rise in price and volatility -- an assumption at least as likely wrong as right (spreads often widen with volatility) and unverifiable without new data. This is exactly the out-of-domain extrapolation this project has consistently refused elsewhere (AR(1) invalidated for scale, the degenerate wide-SL/TP diagnostic). Declines to pursue CTO's conditional follow-up (deriving an ATR threshold from fixed cost) since it presupposes a real edge the test never established -- building on that premise would mean building on something already rejected in ground one. States the only legitimate path forward: a genuinely new, separately pre-registered hypothesis tested on current data with current cost verified fresh at source, not a retroactive rescaling of an already-rejected result -- explicitly out of scope for this no-new-measurement mandate. The OBDZ line stays CLOSED.

No formal numeric correction built now (n=2-3 has ~zero power to distinguish correlation from real edge regardless of method) -- registered as a standing principle instead: any future formal regime-persistence significance test at larger scale must use a null model accounting for both correlation sources, never the naive m*p^k calculation.

Mandatory pre-screening BEFORE any future multiple-testing correction on any hypothesis-ID corpus: family size (m) must be the deduplicated distinct-strategy count, never the raw ID count.

re_arming_bug_MK02.defect: detect_breaks's activation loop re-assigns live_hh/live_ll at every bar without excluding already-consumed swings, contradicting its own docstring ('a swing is consumed by the first break, never reused'). Reproduction: a single HH produces multiple BOS_BULL breaks (VE: 3, referencing idx6; CEO's independent repro: 4, referencing idx7) all pointing at the same already-broken swing, instead of exactly one.
re_arming_bug_MK02.fix_rule: Maintain an explicit consumed set/flag on the Swing record itself (not merely nulling a downstream live_hh/live_ll pointer). A swing enters the consumed set the instant a break is recorded against it. The activation loop must FILTER the candidate pool to exclude consumed swings BEFORE selecting/assigning live_hh/live_ll -- filtering happens at the pool/index level, upstream of assignment, never as a downstream nulling that the next iteration can silently overwrite. A consumed swing never re-enters the active pool for the remainder of its block (consistent with D3/D4 -- it does not survive a block boundary anyway).

decision.chosen: Option 2 (disjoint test populations) as PRIMARY + option 3's measurement as a MANDATORY SECONDARY. Explicitly NOT option 1.
decision.why_two_options_combined: The ask contains two different questions with different correct answers. SCIENTIFIC: on a displacement-touch bar the reversal thesis ('the level holds') is falsified by the very bar being measured -- a contaminated subpopulation, not a neutral sample, so the sharp test excludes them. OPERATIONAL: the policy as written does trade them, so real behaviour requires including them. The DIFFERENCE between the two measurements IS the measured cost of the missing exclusion -- option 3's substance delivered as a byproduct of a clean test rather than instead of one, at zero extra data cost (same events, two partitions).
decision.why_not_option_1: A mechanism change belongs to Alpha, not the Statistician -- honored. The mandatory secondary measurement produces exactly the evidence needed for that decision; it is neither pre-authorized nor pre-excluded.
decision.declared_weakness: The TESTED population (disjoint) is not the TRADED population (full). A positive primary result does NOT transfer automatically to the policy as written -- which is precisely why the secondary measurement is mandatory, not optional, and why reporting the primary alone is an incomplete reading.
decision.applies_only_to_cand_0001: CAND-0009 is already disjoint by its own construction and is NOT touched. The partition completes without modifying any policy.

dependence_finding_statisticians_own.finding: On overlap bars the two candidates hold OPPOSITE positions on the same bar and instrument, so their per-trade outcomes are approximately sign-flipped there and their test statistics become NEGATIVELY dependent in proportion to the overlap fraction.
dependence_finding_statisticians_own.why_it_decides_the_choice: BH-FDR -- the correction fixed at v2.7.33 -- is proven under independence and PRDS (positive dependence); negative dependence is NOT covered by PRDS and would require Benjamini-Yekutieli, whose threshold tightens by sum(1/i) ~= 2.59x at a family of 7, severely penalizing five candidates with no involvement in the conflict. The disjoint construction removes the shared bars, eliminating the negative dependence BY CONSTRUCTION and RESTORING BH's validity unchanged. This is the decisive argument and it is derived, not a preference: option 2 is the only choice that preserves the already-pre-registered correction method.

CAND_0002_finding_H_sharpened.S2_immunity_verified_not_assumed: The expansion bar (range>1.5xATR, body>=0.5xrange) guarantees a wide stop, so the floor should never bind -- but floored(bool) is reported regardless. If it ever binds here, the structural premise fails and must be investigated, not ignored.

CAND_0003_tightest_gate_two_derived_cons.consequence_1_floor_destroys_structural_: The policy's stated rationale is that the stop IS the ratified Q4 inversion boundary. When min_executable_risk binds (small gaps -- the ROUTINE case, not the tail), the stop widens BEYOND that boundary and is no longer at the inversion point but at an arbitrary distance past it. Applying the floor therefore does not merely resize the position -- it changes what the stop MEANS, and the policy's own structural rationale ceases to hold for those trades. Declared and routed to Alpha/CEO as an interpretation-changing observation; NOT repaired here (that would be redesigning risk).
CAND_0003_tightest_gate_two_derived_cons.consequence_2_floor_collapses_RR_systema: Derived arithmetically: entry at ce_50 makes stop distance = target distance = half the gap height (which is why R:R is ~1 as a geometric consequence, not a choice). But the floor widens ONLY the stop; the target stays fixed at the near edge. So on small gaps: risk = floored (larger), reward = half gap height (unchanged, small) => R:R << 1 SYSTEMATICALLY, worst on the smallest gaps -- precisely the routine population. MANDATORY: floored and unfloored trades reported SEPARATELY with realized R:R per group; pooling would hide a structurally disadvantaged subpopulation under one mean.
CAND_0003_tightest_gate_two_derived_cons.consequence_3_S1_fraction_is_a_validity_: Since one ordinary bar routinely spans both edges of a small gap, a large share of outcomes would be decided by the worst-case tie-break convention rather than by observed market behaviour. MANDATORY: report side by side the fraction resolved UNAMBIGUOUSLY (stop only, or target only, on different bars) and the fraction resolved BY THE S1 HIERARCHY. No numeric cutoff invented; the interpretive rule is stated instead -- if the S1-resolved fraction is comparable to or exceeds the unambiguous one, the DEMO result is determined mostly by a convention, not by the market, and must be read as such rather than as evidence about the mechanism.
CAND_0003_tightest_gate_two_derived_cons.red_team_gate_verbatim: If the DEMO engine cannot be shown to apply the floor + worst-case convention, CAND-0003 must NOT trade -- small FVGs make both defects the common case, not the tail.

CAND_0007_risk_reward.planned_RR_computable_at_entry: Both the combined stop (min/max of the two structural floors) and the target (opposite prior-day level) are known AT ENTRY, so risk-reward is computable before entering. MANDATORY per-trade declared field: planned_RR = |target-entry| / executable_stop_distance (on the FLOORED distance). Aggregate: the planned_RR distribution plus the fraction below 1.
CAND_0007_risk_reward.no_filter_imposed: Declines to impose a 'no trade if R:R<1' rule -- that would be a new ENTRY condition, hence a risk method, hence Alpha's. Measured and routed instead; if the sub-1 fraction is material, Alpha/CEO have the factual basis to decide a filter.
CAND_0007_risk_reward.symmetry_with_CAND_0003_noted: At CAND-0003 the floor degrades R:R by widening the stop; at CAND-0007 R:R can fall below 1 by construction (wide combined stop + opposite-level target). Different causes, same measurable consequence -- hence the same planned_RR reporting format, comparable across both.
CAND_0007_risk_reward.S2_protection_verified_not_assumed: The combined stop is the deeper of two floors, hence wider, hence the floor rarely binds -- but floored(bool) is reported regardless.
CAND_0007_risk_reward.W_incr_extended_to_the_risk_layer: Red Team observed that CAND-0007's Part B reuses CAND-0001's exit while its entry zone is a subset of CAND-0003's. The W-incr incremental test already specified at STAT-BATCH-A-0001 must therefore now cover RISK as well as entry -- otherwise apparent confluence value could arise entirely from the wider stop rather than from the confluence. A precision added to the existing protocol, not a new protocol.
