These three DO belong to the family of 7 for future formal tests, but DEMO consumes none of it because it runs no test. No DEMO figure promotes anything; a positive one is not even a candidate requiring pre-registration.
batch_b_0002_demo_criteria_v2_7_36.routed_to_alpha_ceo_none_decided_here: (1) a forward-computable horizon term for CAND-0002; (2) the observation that the floor changes the stop's structural meaning at CAND-0003; (3) whether an R:R filter is wanted at CAND-0007.
batch_b_0002_demo_criteria_v2_7_36.handoff: Validation Engine -- executability plus mechanical gate verification per candidate, using the named audit fields.
batch_b_0002_demo_criteria_v2_7_36.note_on_separate_item: The CAND-0008/0009/0010 protocols requested as a separate 'when you have capacity' item were ALREADY delivered in the prior mandate (batch_a_0002_partition_and_protocols_v2_7_35) and are not redone. CAND-0011 through 0019 await Red Team Phase A and are not yet in the Statistician's trigger.

realized_cost_reevaluation_protocol_v2_7.status: PROTOCOL ONLY -- NOTHING REOPENED. Specifies what would be required before any verdict could be revisited on a corrected cost. One observation establishes nothing.
realized_cost_reevaluation_protocol_v2_7.measurement_received: First realized round-trip cost on a real DEMO account (FusionMarkets XAUUSD, ticket 499680521): both legs filled at the requested price, zero slippage, observed spread $0.05 at send and at close, account flat afterward. Model uses $0.20 -- a ratio of 0.25.
realized_cost_reevaluation_protocol_v2_7.constant_provenance_verified_at_source: cost_round_trip=0.20 is NOT a measurement. It is a construction: 2*(spread_ticks+slip_ticks)*TICK = 2*(5+5)*0.01, where spread_ticks=5 came from a stated 5-15 tick range and slip_ticks=5 came from an explicit CONVENTION ('slip = spread'), never observed (v2.7.8). This reframes the question.

the_4x_is_two_errors_not_one.spread_half: modeled 0.10 (2x5x0.01) vs observed 0.05 -- roughly 2x over, PASSIVELY MEASURABLE, and the observation bears on it directly.
the_4x_is_two_errors_not_one.slippage_half: modeled 0.10 vs observed 0.00 -- has NO empirical basis whatsoever (a declared convention) and CANNOT be measured by observing spread at all. Slippage materialises at size, on volatile bars and gaps -- exactly the conditions these strategies trigger in. A single calm, minimum-size fill with zero slippage says almost nothing about it.
the_4x_is_two_errors_not_one.consistency_note: The observed 5 ticks sits at the LOW end of the originally-stated 5-15 tick range, not the middle -- exactly what a calm-moment sample looks like. This frames the observation rather than undermining it.
the_4x_is_two_errors_not_one.commission_check_required: A $0.05 gold spread implies a raw/ECN account, which typically charges commission separately. If so, the true round-trip cost is 0.05 + commission and the cited figure is not the full cost. To be VERIFIED at the account-spec source, not assumed -- same discipline as the original TICK verification.

Q1_sampling.estimand: NOT the mean spread. The mean cost CONDITIONAL ON A TRADE TRIGGERING. Cost enters expectancy linearly so the mean (not median) is correct -- but trades do not occur at random moments. They cluster on volatility events (expansion bars, level touches, gaps) where spreads widen, so E[cost|trigger] > E[cost|random calendar moment].
Q1_sampling.sampling_answer: Neither purely random nor purely stratified: continuous collection is the right raw mechanism, but the ESTIMATE must be reweighted to the trigger distribution rather than the calendar distribution -- which is only possible if the stratification labels are recorded alongside each observation.
Q1_sampling.strata_already_ratified: 4 sessions (session_of) x 3 volatility states (compression/normal/expansion, market_state) = 12 cells. Reuses ratified primitives and the same 3-state partition already specified at v2.7.30; nothing invented.
Q1_sampling.effective_n_is_days_not_ticks: DECISIVE TECHNICAL POINT: 30-second observations are massively autocorrelated -- 2880 readings per day are nowhere near 2880 independent observations, and a CI computed on tick-count would be absurdly narrow and falsely confident. Sampling unit = (day x session); mean and CI estimated by cluster/block bootstrap over DAYS, reusing the already-ratified block_bootstrap mechanics. Threshold: n>=25 DISTINCT DAYS per cell (the standing N_MIN convention applied to the correct unit). Honestly implies weeks-to-months of collection, and rare cells (e.g. expansion during asia) fill last.
Q1_sampling.stopping_rule_derived_not_invented: No precision target invented. Criterion: the ENTIRE 95% CI (cluster bootstrap, trigger-reweighted) must lie BELOW 0.20 for the model to be demonstrated wrong. If the CI straddles 0.20, collection continues.

Q2_which_verdicts.correction_to_the_stated_reason: The mandate says edge_brut carries the cost error additively. Verified otherwise at v2.7.24: edge_brut_dollars - expectancy_dollars = exactly 0.20 in all three regimes, so edge_brut = expectancy + assumed_cost while expectancy = raw - assumed_cost, and the two cancel -- edge_brut reconstructs RAW GROSS and is arithmetically cost-independent. The REAL obstacle is populational and non-additive: cost sets the ATR eligibility floor (3xcost/SL_mult) and min_executable_risk (k_spread x effective_spread), which jointly determine WHICH trades enter the sample. Change cost -> change floor -> change population -> different gross edge on a different event set. 'Do not recompute' is correct, for a stronger reason than the one given.
Q2_which_verdicts.decisive_temporal_constraint: At v2.7.25 an ATR-rescaling inference was rejected partly BECAUSE it extrapolated a present-day figure onto historical data. A present-day cost measurement is the SAME category of inference, in the favorable direction. Rejecting that inference when unfavorable and accepting it when favorable would be a double standard. Therefore: a current measurement establishes CURRENT cost and does NOT, by itself, reopen any historical backtest verdict. Acknowledged asymmetry: a mechanical constant is genuinely stronger evidence than a behavioral edge -- but evidential strength does not solve the temporal problem; a good measurement of the wrong thing remains a measurement of the wrong thing.
Q2_which_verdicts.category_A_cost_decisive_REOPENABLE: OBDZ-002 REJECTED_AT_DECLARED_PARAMETRIZATION -- YES, cost-sensitive: gross was POSITIVE in every regime (+0.166/+0.050/+0.471) and cost consumed it in bear/bull; a lower cost shifts the whole net_R distribution upward and would move p-values materially. The deliberately scoped label ('at the DECLARED parametrization') already anticipated revisability. Same category structurally for the S-family rejections killed net-of-cost.
Q2_which_verdicts.category_B_other_reason_NOT_REOPENED: SMC_S1 STATISTICALLY REJECTED (v2.7.9) -- does NOT reopen on this argument. Its decisive reason was that gross edge was near-zero with INCONSISTENT SIGN across regimes. A lower cost subtracts less; it cannot manufacture an edge that was never reliably positive. Honest caveat: the floor->population channel means the sample would have differed, so strictly it would require a re-run -- but that is a NEW TEST consuming family, not a free reopening.
Q2_which_verdicts.category_C_no_cost_dependence_UNTOUCHED: The MFE zone-vs-pullback signal (v2.7.21, +0.232xATR, n=654) was measured on RAW price excursions with no cost term at all -- it neither strengthens nor weakens. Also untouched: D1-D7 ratifications, the MK-01/MK-02 fidelity review, the block_bootstrap calibration, and the ATR-rescaling rejection itself.
Q2_which_verdicts.linking_observation: The only POSITIVE finding in this entire line never depended on cost; every failure was in CONVERTING it to net-of-cost profit. If cost really is several times lower, that conversion problem shrinks -- but that remains a hypothesis to test, not a conclusion, and only for the period in which cost was actually measured.
Q2_which_verdicts.three_cumulative_conditions: (1) the whole 95% CI below 0.20; (2) the TEMPORAL problem addressed -- either historical spread data for 2011-2022, or an explicit, declared re-framing of the verdicts as being about FORWARD performance rather than the historical backtest (a change of object, not a silent slide); (3) the SLIPPAGE component measured on REAL fills. All three, not the first alone -- condition (2) is the hardest and the easiest to skip quietly.

Q3_constant_or_variable.left_empirical_with_the_test_pre_specifi: Not decided a priori. Estimate the elasticity of observed spread to contemporaneous ATR14 (and session) via regression/binning on a log-log slope. Elasticity ~0 => cost IS a dollar constant; keep the current form with a corrected value, and the v2.7.24 finding stands. Elasticity ~1 => cost scales with ATR => cost/R is roughly CONSTANT => the advantage of high-ATR regimes DISAPPEARS.
Q3_constant_or_variable.own_conclusion_placed_at_risk: At v2.7.24 the OBDZ failure was explained structurally as fixed cost versus ATR-scaled edge -- which is why bull, with the lowest ATR, could never clear cost. If elasticity comes out near 1, THAT EXPLANATION IS WRONG and must be revised, and the v2.7.25 ATR-rescaling rejection gains a fourth independent reason (cost would rise with ATR, cancelling the supposed gain). Criterion written before seeing the data.

Q4_collection.passive_fields: Per observation: UTC timestamp, bid, ask, spread=(ask-bid), mid. MANDATORY labels without which the Q1 reweighting is impossible: session (session_of), volatility state (compression/expansion), contemporaneous M15 ATR14 (indispensable for Q3), and day (for the Q1 clustering). No orders, no cost incurred.
Q4_collection.what_passive_observation_cannot_give: Slippage and commission are invisible in bid/ask -- they appear only in real fills. Separately mandatory per REAL DEMO order: requested vs filled price on BOTH legs, realized slippage per leg, commission if any, order size, and the same labels. Explicitly: slippage observed in calm conditions at minimum size does NOT extrapolate to these strategies' trigger conditions. Until real fills exist IN those conditions, the slippage half of the model remains unverified -- and it is the half with no empirical basis at all.
Q4_collection.connection_to_existing_demo_gates: min_executable_risk uses k_spread x effective_spread, and effective_spread was already mandated (v2.7.34/v2.7.36) to be the REALIZED value rather than an assumed one. This collection is precisely what feeds that field -- not a parallel measurement but the source of a value already required. A real spread of 0.05 instead of an assumed 0.40 CHANGES THE FLOOR, hence changes how many trades are floored at CAND-0003, directly connected to the consequence derived at v2.7.36.

realized_cost_reevaluation_protocol_v2_7.what_does_not_change_regardless: Holdout stays sealed. Family stays 7. No re-run is free: a re-run under a corrected cost is a NEW TEST on the same data and CONSUMES family. Stated now, because otherwise a corrected cost becomes an unlimited re-test door for everything that has failed.
realized_cost_reevaluation_protocol_v2_7.handoff: AI Trader -- passive collection with the labeled fields. Validation Engine -- real-fill capture plus commission verification at the account source. Statistician -- resumes when n>=25 distinct days per cell is reached, or earlier if the commission check changes the base figure.

mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.status: SEMANTICS SPECIFIED for detect_breaks cascade timing (CEO decision, after RT-CODE-A-0002 §4). D2 and D7 unchanged. Handoff: VE implements + measures cascade frequency, Red Team re-attacks, then final ratification.
mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.two_staggering_vectors_not_one: The current behaviour staggers for TWO independent reasons and the fix must cover both: (a) the single-slot live_* pointers retain only the MOST RECENT swing of each label, so other active same-label swings are never even evaluated at bar c; (b) the within-direction if/elif suppresses an exceeded LH whenever an HH breaks on the same bar. RT-CODE-A-0002 named only (a).
mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.specification: For each bar c: (1) active = swings with confirmed_idx < c AND idx not in consumed (upstream filtering, the re-arm patch mechanic, UNCHANGED); (2) evaluate close[c] against ALL active members, not only the most recent -- BOS_BULL for every active HH with px > price, CHOCH_BULL for every active LH with px > price, BOS_BEAR for every active LL with px < price, CHOCH_BEAR for every active HL with px < price; (3) emit one StructureBreak with idx=c for EACH qualifying swing; (4) consume all qualifying idx in the SAME step before advancing. Strict inequalities unchanged (D2). Each distinct swing still produces exactly one break, never re-armed (D7) -- only the BAR IT IS RECORDED ON changes.
mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.consequence_the_example_does_not_show: The mandate's two-stacked-HH example illustrates only vector (a), same-label. The decision AS WORDED ('all swings exceeded by close[c] break at bar c') also covers vector (b), cross-label: an exceeded LH is an exceeded swing. Implemented as worded, but flagged explicitly -- from now a BOS_BULL and a CHOCH_BULL can occur on the SAME bar against distinct reference swings (an HH and an LH), where the second was previously suppressed. NOT double-counting: two events on two distinct references, exactly what 'one break per distinct swing' requires. Named as a conscious change to an existing precedence, for Red Team to attack, rather than left as a silent side effect.
mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.count_is_not_strictly_conserved_and_the_: The elif did not merely delay -- it could DROP a break permanently. Example: close[c]=120 exceeds HH=110 and LH=115; today BOS fires and the CHoCH is suppressed, and if close falls to 112 at c+1 the CHoCH never occurs at all. Under the new semantics both fire at c. So the new semantics yields MORE breaks in the lapse case -- NOT a change to D7, but the delivery of what D7 already specified ('each distinct swing produces one') and which the one-break-per-bar artifact under-delivered.

intra_bar_ordering.it_matters_for_a_concrete_existing_consu: trading_strategies.py::_first_break_after selects via a strict 'b.idx < best.idx' comparison, which CANNOT separate breaks that now share idx=c -- whichever appears first in the list wins. This situation never arose before, since one break per bar per kind was guaranteed. List order therefore becomes semantically load-bearing.
intra_bar_ordering.rule: Breaks emitted at bar c are ordered DESCENDING by reference_swing.idx (most recent exceeded swing first). idx is unique per swing (verified: detect_swings emits at most one Swing per bar index, the is_high/is_low branches being mutually exclusive via continue), so the order is TOTAL with no tie-break required.
intra_bar_ordering.why_descending_is_derived_not_aesthetic: In the current code live_hh retains the LAST HH traversed, i.e. the MOST RECENT, so today's break at bar c already references the most recent exceeded swing. Descending order keeps exactly that reference in first position, so existing consumers receive the SAME reference_swing as before and the change stays strictly one of TIMING, not of reference. Ascending order would have silently changed the reference too.
intra_bar_ordering.the_semantic_choice_underneath_is_not_th: _first_break_after feeds reference_swing.price as 'the broken BOS level' (e.g. S2's spike distance). With several levels broken on one bar, 'which is the level' becomes a STRATEGY question -- nearest or furthest. The ordering rule above defaults to nearest for continuity, but the owner of trading_strategies.py must confirm that deliberately rather than inherit it from an ordering default. Flagged, not decided here.
intra_bar_ordering.hygiene_rule_for_future_consumers: Intra-bar order is for DETERMINISM/reproducibility only and encodes no significance. Any consumer needing 'the most significant break' must compute it from price, never from list position.

mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.F4_not_resolved_and_its_surface_grows: F4 (RT-CODE-A-0001 §5: the bullish and bearish blocks run independently on the same close, so a crossed LH/HL can emit contradictory CHOCH_BULL and CHOCH_BEAR on one bar) remains OPEN and is NOT resolved here -- resolving it would exceed the CEO's decision and change semantics beyond timing. But flagged: since each direction can now emit MULTIPLE breaks per bar, the number of possible contradictory pairs on a single bar INCREASES. The timing fix does not create F4 but widens its surface -- relevant to the Red Team re-attack and the final ratification.

what_is_affected_premise_corrected.verified_not_accepted: The mandate's premise ('MK-01 detectors were used in no candidate, so nothing re-runs') is TRUE for the candidates and FALSE in general.
what_is_affected_premise_corrected.candidates_genuinely_clean: institutional_levels.py and imbalance_mechanics.py both import ONLY Block from market_structure; market_state, interactions and order_block_void import it not at all. No CAND-000x touches detect_breaks.
what_is_affected_premise_corrected.but_trading_strategies_does: code/trading_strategies.py calls detect_breaks at four sites: line 173 (detect_s2), 203 (detect_s3), 276 (detect_s10), 305 (detect_s11).
what_is_affected_premise_corrected.and_the_consumption_is_timing_sensitive: _first_break_after filters on 'lo < b.idx <= hi' -- a 20-bar Group-A qualification window anchored on the break index. A break displaced by up to N-1 bars can move INTO or OUT OF that window, changing not merely the entry bar but the ELIGIBILITY of the setup itself.
what_is_affected_premise_corrected.conclusion: The already-measured descriptive results for S2, S3 and S11 consumed detect_breaks output and are in principle affected (S10 is excluded anyway -- open re-loop). VERIFIED UNAFFECTED: detect_s1 does NOT call detect_breaks, so the SMC_S1 STATISTICALLY REJECTED verdict stands untouched, as do S7, S13, S16, S17.
what_is_affected_premise_corrected.magnitude_calibrated_not_overstated: It is NOT claimed that S2/S3/S11 are materially wrong. The cascade requires >=2 same-label active unconsumed swings exceeded by one close -- Red Team confirms it is reachable but also that it is never exercised by any test, so its frequency is UNKNOWN. Correct order: (1) VE implements; (2) VE MEASURES cascade frequency on discovery data (how often one bar breaks >=2 active swings); (3) only THEN decide whether S2/S3/S11 need re-running. If the frequency is negligible, nothing re-runs and the finding stands recorded. If not, the re-run is an EXECUTION CORRECTION on the same hypothesis, hence NOT family-consuming. No re-run is triggered here -- but 'nothing re-runs' cannot be asserted before step (2).

mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.unchanged_reconfirmed: D2 (strict inequalities both sides) untouched. D7 for pools (liquidity_mechanics, consumption at first sweep) untouched -- a different module. The F3 ordering precondition untouched, including Red Team's separate open finding that it is over-strict (global versus per-block). The upstream `consumed` filtering untouched -- it is the very mechanic step 1 relies on.
mk01_cascade_break_semantics_v2_7_38.handoff: VE implements the semantics AND measures cascade frequency in the same pass (cheap, and it settles the only open question). Red Team re-attacks with three explicitly named targets: BOS+CHoCH co-occurrence on one bar, the now semantically-loaded intra-bar order for _first_break_after, and F4's widened surface. Then final ratification.

mk01_mk02_ratification_v2_7_39.status: RATIFIED (CEO). MK-01 market_structure.py and MK-02 liquidity_mechanics.py are RATIFIED -- Alpha may build on them. Three non-blocking open items attached below.
mk01_mk02_ratification_v2_7_39.chain_complete: D1-D7 fidelity 7/7 (v2.7.31) -> VE executability + F2/F3 remediation -> Red Team re-attack (RT-CODE-A-0001, RT-CODE-A-0002) -> cascade semantics specified and implemented (v2.7.38) -> measurement confirming scale -> CEO ratification.
mk01_mk02_ratification_v2_7_39.measurement_verified_directly: Read reports/cascade_frequency_results.json (commit 0000225) and recomputed the aggregates: 18,961 break-bars of which 7,752 carried >=2 breaks = 40.9% (exact), maximum 24 breaks on one bar (exact), 542 breaks lost forever under the old semantics (exact).
mk01_mk02_ratification_v2_7_39.internal_consistency_check_added: breaks_new - breaks_old = 34,731 - 34,189 = 542, matching refs_lost_forever_under_old to the unit. The two figures are derived independently in the report and coincide exactly. This EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMS the prediction derived at v2.7.38 that the elif was DROPPING breaks rather than merely delaying them, and that the count increase is precisely the lost set rather than inflation of another kind. The prediction was theoretical; it is now measured.
mk01_mk02_ratification_v2_7_39.ordering_rule_is_load_bearing_frozen: VE's conclusion that zero of four consumer sites change their reference swing is CONFIRMED -- but the stated reason is sharpened, because the wording matters for the future. The 'kind filter' argument alone is NOT sufficient: two breaks of the SAME kind can now land on one bar, and _first_break_after's 'b.idx < best.idx' is STRICT, so it cannot separate them and the first in list order wins. The operative reason is the second clause (tie behaviour unchanged), and that holds precisely BECAUSE the descending-order-by-reference_swing.idx rule was specified at v2.7.38 to keep the most recent swing in first position, exactly what live_hh emitted before. CONSEQUENCE: the descending-order rule is LOAD-BEARING, not incidental -- if ordering ever changes, the reference changes silently in S2/S3/S10/S11. Frozen as an invariant, with a dedicated test (T2 below).

open_1_F4.position: F4 is NOT a detector defect. When live_lh.price < close[c] < live_hl.price (a crossed structure, contracting-triangle apex), both CHOCH_BULL and CHOCH_BEAR are true statements about the bar. The ambiguity lives in the LABELLED STRUCTURE, not in detection -- the detector faithfully reports a structurally contradictory state. Arbitrarily suppressing one side would HIDE a real ambiguity and reintroduce exactly the class of artifact just eliminated (a precedence rule that erases a true event). Therefore: not resolved inside the detector; both are emitted.
open_1_F4.downstream_rule: Any consumer receiving CHOCH_BULL and CHOCH_BEAR on the same bar: DEFAULT is fail-closed -- NO signal on that bar. An alternative rule is permitted but must be DECLARED explicitly, auditable, and pre-registered alongside the hypothesis using it -- never an implicit default buried in code. The default follows this lab's established fail-closed convention for unresolvable ambiguity (FAIL-CLOSED triggers at CAND-0004/0005/0006, after=0 pinned at CAND-0007, INVALID_EXECUTION on ambiguous fills).
open_1_F4.measurement_required: F4 frequency is NOT measured. The cascade was (40.9%); F4 additionally requires a crossed structure. Required in the same pass: how many bars emit CHOCH_BULL and CHOCH_BEAR simultaneously, per regime, absolute and as a fraction of break-bars. Without that figure 'non-blocking' is an assumption; with it, a fact.

open_2_four_missing_tests.T1_F4: Crossed structure (LH.price < HL.price), close between them. ASSERT both CHOCH_BULL and CHOCH_BEAR emitted at the same bar, both consumed, ordering deterministic. Pins the behaviour; does not resolve it.
open_2_four_missing_tests.T2_reference_selection: STAR -- most important of the four. >=2 breaks of the SAME kind on one bar. ASSERT _first_break_after returns the MOST RECENT swing. Converts the descending-order rule from a convention into an ENFORCED INVARIANT, so a future reordering breaks a test instead of silently changing S2/S3/S10/S11 semantics.
open_2_four_missing_tests.T3_aggregate_conservation: STAR -- highest diagnostic power. Over a whole block, ASSERT break count = number of distinct swings ever exceeded while active; none lost, none doubled. This is EXACTLY the invariant the old defect violated (542 lost) and that no suite checked.
open_2_four_missing_tests.T4_high_multiplicity: One bar breaking >=24 stacked swings (the MEASURED maximum). ASSERT all emitted at that bar, all consumed, total ordering, no truncation or off-by-one at scale. Existing tests reach at most 3; reality produced 24.
open_2_four_missing_tests.status: Requested of VE. Ratification is not conditional on them (CEO decided), but the coverage gap stays RECORDED until delivered -- not closed silently.

open_3_rerun_S2_S3_S11.cause_accepted: VE established it correctly: not a reference shift (T2/ordering prevent that) but a change in the SET of breaks -- 542 breaks that did not exist at all under the old semantics now do, plus thousands relocated to the correct bar. Genuinely NEW setups appear, not merely displaced ones. With the 20-bar eligibility window anchored on the break index, a new or moved break changes ELIGIBILITY, not just entry timing.
open_3_rerun_S2_S3_S11.remains_execution_correction_not_family_: The hypothesis is unchanged -- S2 remains 'BOS then opposite CHoCH within 20 bars, fade'. The detector under-delivered events the hypothesis always covered. Repairing the implementation and re-running is NOT a second attempt on the same data; it is the FIRST CORRECT run. Family stays 7, untouched.
open_3_rerun_S2_S3_S11.pre_commitment_that_keeps_it_true: The real risk is behavioural, not conceptual: a re-run yielding better figures could retrospectively become 'we fixed it until it worked'. Prevented by pre-commitment written BEFORE the re-run: SCOPE = exactly S2, S3, S11 (the three that consume detect_breaks and have measured results); S10 EXCLUDED (open re-loop, already excluded); S1/S7/S13/S16/S17 NOT touched (verified: they do not call detect_breaks). WHAT = identical metrics, regimes, cost and floor as the original run; NOTHING else changes alongside the detector. HOW = the new result REPLACES the old in EITHER direction, including worse; both retained in the record with the delta. REPORTED = mandatory old-vs-new n per family and regime, so the population change is visible rather than buried in a mean. FORBIDDEN = any other parameter change taking advantage of the re-run.

session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.status: SPECIFICATION (second task of the same mandate). Mechanical spec for session High/Low/Mid plus a touch detector. Nothing implemented; neither lifetime variant preferred -- both to be measured separately.
session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.session_instance: A maximal run of consecutive bars sharing the same session label, WITHIN a block; terminates at a label change OR a block boundary (D3_bis), whichever comes first. Obtained with the EXISTING _runs helper applied to market_state.sessions(time) instead of day_index -- zero new segmentation code.
session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.clock_misalignment_flagged_not_assumed_a: Sessions run on UTC hours (asia<8, london<13, ny<21, late) while the day anchor is 17:00 NY (21:00/22:00 UTC, DST-dependent), so a 'late' instance CAN straddle a day_index boundary. Cutting on days is NOT imposed -- neither D3_bis nor lookahead-freedom requires it, and it would fragment instances and multiply levels. Instead a MANDATORY diagnostic: how often an instance crosses a day boundary. Plus a second: the distribution of instance lengths, since a block-truncated instance can be 1 bar, giving High=Low and a degenerate Mid -- mechanically valid but to be reported so a policy can exclude them explicitly rather than silently.
session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.Q1_which_session_uses_whose_levels: The PRIMITIVE is GENERAL: every closed instance emits its 3 levels, available from the next instance in the same block, each tagged with source_session and the source instance index. The RESTRICTION belongs to POLICY. Grounded in the ratified Module-7 precedent (v2.6.1): interactions.py was ratified as a GENERIC locator with the explicit rule that a specific combination is a HYPOTHESIS requiring separate pre-registration -- freezing 'Asia to London only' into the primitive would embed a hypothesis choice inside infrastructure, which that ruling forbids. The classic Asia-to-London case stays fully expressible as a DECLARED policy filter, where it is auditable. Anti-proliferation control: any candidate built on these levels must report trigger counts broken down by source_session.
session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.Q2_availability: available_idx = the FIRST BAR OF THE NEXT INSTANCE (the bar immediately after the source instance's last bar) -- identical to PDH/PDL's Q4 convention, literally the same construction. No lookahead by construction: High/Low are known only after the source instance's final bar closes, and Mid=(High+Low)/2 derives solely from them, adding no temporal requirement. D3_bis: the first instance in each block has no predecessor and emits nothing.

Q3_two_distinct_lifetime_primitives.A_SESSION_BOUNDED: Active window [available_idx, last bar of the NEXT instance]; expires at that instance's end whether touched or not. ~3 active at a time (H/L/Mid of one source instance) -- bounded by construction, analogous to PDH/PDL.
Q3_two_distinct_lifetime_primitives.B_SESSION_PERSISTENT: Active window [available_idx, first touch (D7) OR block end], whichever comes first. UNBOUNDED by construction -- accumulates with every untouched instance.
Q3_two_distinct_lifetime_primitives.mandatory_control_on_B: The risk is known and already quantified: DZ x FVG produced 18,275 trades and -$2,432 -- too many zones, each worthless -- and that failure was discovered only AFTER those 18,275 trades were generated. The preventive is cheap and imposed now: BEFORE any candidate is built on B, measure as a standalone diagnostic (i) the distribution of ACTIVE level count per bar, per regime (mean, median, max), and (ii) the total touch count B would produce, per regime. If (i) grows monotonically without a ceiling and (ii) is in the thousands, the DZ x FVG pattern is repeating -- and it is known BEFORE, not after. B is not forbidden (it is legitimate, and price genuinely can react to a months-old Asia Mid); only its structural price must be visible before it is paid.

session_levels_spec_v2_7_39.Q4_consumption: DEFAULT D7 -- first touch consumes, no re-arm. Consistent with EVERY ratified level primitive here (detect_level_touches Q5/D7, OB mitigation, pool sweeps); deviating without evidence would be an inconsistency, not an improvement. KNOWN LIMITATION recorded not hidden: Red Team already established (RT-CODE-A-0001, D7 section) that this convention makes a genuine SECOND reaction at the same level invisible -- it applies identically here. The re-arm alternative stays mentioned-but-unimplemented, exactly the treatment given D2/D7 at the original ratification.

Q5_touch_detector_Mid_is_a_different_cla.structural_distinction_added: High and Low are LIQUIDITY levels -- stops rest beyond them, which is the mechanism the entire MK-04 family rests on. Mid is a geometric midpoint: NO liquidity rests there. Different classes of object with different reaction mechanisms.
Q5_touch_detector_Mid_is_a_different_cla.touch_definitions: High: high[j] >= price (resistance, one-sided, as PDH). Low: low[j] <= price (support, one-sided, as PDL). Mid: low[j] <= price <= high[j] (the bar's RANGE CONTAINS the level).
Q5_touch_detector_Mid_is_a_different_cla.Mid_has_no_intrinsic_side: Mid can be approached from either direction, so trade DIRECTION CANNOT come from the level, unlike PDH(short)/PDL(long). Any policy using Mid must DECLARE how direction is determined (bias, approach direction, or otherwise) -- it cannot inherit the PDH/PDL convention, which does not apply.
Q5_touch_detector_Mid_is_a_different_cla.mandatory_separate_reporting: High, Low and Mid reported SEPARATELY, never pooled. The mechanisms differ; a common average would hide exactly the difference that matters.
Q5_touch_detector_Mid_is_a_different_cla.rest_mirrors_existing: Availability window from available_idx, block-bounded (D4), consumed at first touch (D7), forward-only iteration -- detect_level_touches verbatim.

three_reaction_detectors_spec_v2_7_40.status: SPECIFICATION for detect_void_reactions, detect_bpr_reactions, detect_weekly_level_touches -- unblocking CAND-0004/0005/0006. Nothing implemented. CAND-0006 requires RE-FRAMING, not merely unblocking (see below).
three_reaction_detectors_spec_v2_7_40.approach: All three mirror already-ratified conventions rather than inventing parallels, following the session_levels.py precedent (which passed Red Team on the first attempt).

PWH_PWL_decisive_finding.method: Asked to say BEFORE construction whether a weekly touch detector could yield a usable population, MEASURED it rather than estimating -- temporary uncommitted script, deleted after use, reusing only ratified primitives and the existing survey's own load path.
PWH_PWL_decisive_finding.funnel_measured: Across the three discovery regimes: (1) 572 weekly levels emitted, 538 COMPLETE; (2) 275 touched geometrically = 48.1%, ENTIRELY HEALTHY; (3) only 6 also bias-aligned = 2.2% of touched. Per regime 3/2/1 -- reproducing the survey's n=6 and its exact regime split, confirming this decomposes the SAME population rather than a different one.
PWH_PWL_decisive_finding.cause_is_structural_not_statistical: The collapse is entirely at the bias stage. A WEEKLY_HIGH can only be touched by price rallying UP to reach it, yet its trade direction is SHORT (resistance), requiring H1 AND H4 bias both DOWN. The two conditions contradict each other by construction: arriving at a weekly extreme essentially means the trend on comparable horizons runs the other way. Confirmed directly by the counts -- highs touched 147 times, aligned 2; lows touched 128 times, aligned 4.
PWH_PWL_decisive_finding.generalization_with_a_testable_predictio: For ANY prior-period-extreme level, 'touched' and 'bias-aligned for REVERSAL' are structurally anti-correlated, and the anti-correlation WORSENS as the period lengthens (daily weak: PDH/PDL n=356; weekly severe: n=6). PREDICTION: sub-daily SESSION levels should be affected LESS than daily ones, being closer and touched in both directions -- cheap to verify at the first session_levels.py measurement.
PWH_PWL_decisive_finding.operational_conclusion: BUILD the weekly detector: it works and yields 275 usable events. But RE-FRAME CAND-0006 rather than merely unblocking it -- the degeneracy was never the detector's fault. Three re-framings offered, none chosen (Alpha's decision): (a) bias supplies DIRECTION rather than eligibility; (b) inverted thesis -- continuation THROUGH the level rather than reversal FROM it, which would align naturally with the move that produces the touch; (c) no bias at all, as a pure test of the level. Population available for (a)/(c) is 275, not 6. The common diagnosis that a missing detector blocked CAND-0006 was wrong.

detect_void_reactions.mirrors: detect_fvg_reactions' ratified three-tier Q6 gradient -- a void is the same class of object (a skipped price interval). Zero new convention.
detect_void_reactions.inputs: Voids from detect_liquidity_voids plus the zone/polarity derived at v2.7.27: zone=[min(close[c],open[c+1]), max(...)], mid=midpoint, polarity BULLISH if open[c+1]>close[c] (gap up, acts as support below) else BEARISH. available_idx=c+1 (both terms known then, Red-Team verified).
detect_void_reactions.three_tier_gradient: Each an OPTIONAL first-occurrence index: partial_fill_idx = first bar reaching MID (bull low[j]<=mid / bear high[j]>=mid); full_fill_idx = first bar traversing the zone (bull low[j]<=lower / bear high[j]>=upper); rejection_idx = first bar that ENTERS and CLOSES back outside (bull low[j]<=upper AND close[j]>upper; bear symmetric).
detect_void_reactions.rejection_reuses_D6: The rejection test mirrors the D6 wick-sweep-reject signature verbatim (already ratified in liquidity_mechanics) rather than inventing a fourth rejection convention.
detect_void_reactions.D7_and_windows: As with FVG: each of the three recorded at FIRST occurrence only; the void is consumed as a TRIGGER at first partial_fill; no re-arm. The known D7 limitation (a genuine second reaction is invisible) applies identically and is recorded, not hidden. Selection ends at available_idx=c+1; measurement runs from the reaction bar forward; entry at next-open after it -- disjoint by construction (anti-E010), block-bounded (D3_bis/D4).

detect_bpr_reactions.inputs: Bull-by-bear FVG pairs from count_bpr plus the zone derived at v2.7.27: zone=[max(lower_a,lower_b), min(upper_a,upper_b)], formation=max(formed_idx), available_idx=max(confirmed_idx_a, confirmed_idx_b) so BOTH are confirmed. Tolerance 0.0 strict first, escalating only if n<25 -- the rule already fixed at v2.7.27.
detect_bpr_reactions.no_polarity_resolved_via_entry_side: CONFIRMED that direction comes from bias and the detector must not encode it. But 'complete fill' and 'rejection' need a SIDE to mean anything at all. Resolved by having the detector emit direction-agnostic geometry INCLUDING the entry side: touch_idx = first bar whose range OVERLAPS the zone (containment, as with Mid); entry_side = 'above'/'below', determined causally from close[j-1] relative to the zone; traverse_idx = first bar crossing fully from entry_side to the opposite side; reject_idx = first bar entering and closing back on the ENTRY side (D6 verbatim). entry_side is the piece that makes traversal and rejection interpretable without an intrinsic polarity; the policy combines entry_side with bias and MUST declare that rule -- it cannot inherit the PDH/PDL convention, which presumes an intrinsic side. Same treatment Mid received in session_levels.py.

detect_weekly_level_touches.mirrors: detect_level_touches VERBATIM, with exactly one change: the window is the current WEEK rather than the current day (the same 'if day_index[j] != day: break' structure with week in place of day).
detect_weekly_level_touches.touch_is_exceedance_not_containment: WEEKLY_HIGH: high[j] >= price (resistance, one-sided, as PDH). WEEKLY_LOW: low[j] <= price (support, one-sided, as PDL). EXCEEDANCE, because these are genuine period extremes where liquidity rests -- the same class as PDH/PDL, NOT as Mid. The High/Low-versus-Mid distinction already settled in session_levels.py answers this without a new decision.
detect_weekly_level_touches.D7: Consumed at FIRST touch, no re-arm -- identical to PDH/PDL.
detect_weekly_level_touches.PARTIAL_flag_handling: The detector emits BOTH COMPLETE and PARTIAL weeks and PROPAGATES completeness into the touch record; excluding PARTIAL is a DECLARED policy choice, never a hidden filter in the primitive. But separate reporting is MANDATORY on a derived ground: a PARTIAL week's High/Low are computed over FEWER days, so its extremes are systematically LESS extreme (a 3-day max is below a 5-day max), hence CLOSER to price, hence touched MORE often -- pooling would artificially inflate the touch rate. Same logic as the High/Low/Mid separation. Measured split: 538 COMPLETE, 34 PARTIAL.

three_reaction_detectors_spec_v2_7_40.handoff: VE implements the three detectors (mirroring detect_fvg_reactions / detect_level_touches / D6, no parallel conventions) and, at the first session-levels measurement, checks the Part-0 prediction that sessions should suffer less than daily. Red Team attacks. Alpha RE-FRAMES CAND-0006 before resuming it -- the real population is 275, not 6, but only without the bias-reversal filter.

primitive_b_density_filter_v2_7_41.status: FILTER SPECIFIED and MEASURED. Pre-declared primary k=1.0 PASSES the pre-declared threshold: 188 -> 6 max active, 31x reduction. Unblocks primitive B subject to VE re-verification. Nothing implemented; no candidate built.

form_derived_before_touching_data.two_distinct_charges: Red Team's verdict contains TWO charges needing DIFFERENT remedies: (1) DENSITY -- 89 to 188 levels active simultaneously, not a small decidable set; (2) FALSIFIABILITY -- price is always near some level, so the claim is unfalsifiable BY SATURATION.
form_derived_before_touching_data.rank_filters_rejected_a_priori: A RANK filter (nearest-N, most-recent-N) fixes (1) and makes (2) WORSE. Derivable without data: a rank filter ALWAYS returns N levels, so price is near N levels by construction -- saturation is not removed, only hidden at a fixed count. THE DECIDING CRITERION: the filter must be able to return the EMPTY SET. Only a THRESHOLD can; a RANK never can. The empty set is exactly what falsifiability requires -- there must exist bars where the claim has nothing to predict.
form_derived_before_touching_data.age_rejected_as_primary_axis: Separate reason: a short age bound collapses B into A (persistence is B's whole premise), a long one bounds nothing. DISTANCE preserves the premise -- an old, distant level is irrelevant NOW but becomes eligible again if price returns to it.

filter_fixed_before_measurement.rule: A level is eligible at bar j iff available_idx < j (already required), not yet touched (already required, D7), AND abs(level.price - close[j-1]) <= k * ATR14[j-1].
filter_fixed_before_measurement.k_values: k PRIMARY = 1.0; k SENSITIVITY = {0.5, 2.0}. All declared IN ADVANCE, not chosen afterwards.
filter_fixed_before_measurement.why_k_equals_1_is_not_invented: 1.0xATR is the lab's OWN risk unit -- the stop distance used throughout the DEMO line (SL=1.0xATR at OBDZ-002 and all four pilots). A level within 1xATR sits less than one unit of risk from price, hence genuinely reachable within the trade's own horizon. A reused anchor, not a new one.
filter_fixed_before_measurement.no_lookahead_proof: The filter reads at bar j ONLY close[j-1] and ATR14[j-1], both complete BEFORE bar j opens; the level itself already requires available_idx < j. Therefore the eligible set at bar j is fully known before bar j exists -- zero forward information. Deliberately NOT close[j], which would consult the bar being evaluated; the one-bar lag is what makes the filter executable live rather than only in backtest.

primitive_b_density_filter_v2_7_41.effectiveness_threshold_derived_from_mea: median active <= 9 and max active <= 19 -- an order of magnitude below the MEASURED baseline of 89 median / 188 max, so the anchor is derived from an existing published figure rather than invented. Plus: the zero-eligible-bar fraction must be > 0 and reported. That last one gets an INTERPRETIVE RULE rather than an invented numeric cutoff -- if it is near zero, saturation persists regardless of the active count.

measured_not_estimated.scope: Measured directly across all 130,491 discovery bars, 3 regimes (temporary uncommitted script, deleted). The UNFILTERED baseline reproduces Red Team's figures EXACTLY (median 89, max 188), confirming the same object is being filtered.
measured_not_estimated.results: UNFILTERED: median 89, mean 94, max 188, zero-eligible bars 0.0%, touches 16,578. k=0.5: median 0, max 4, zero 95.3%, touches 3,932 (23.7%). k=1.0 PRIMARY: median 0, mean 0.19, p90 1, max 6, zero 83.6%, touches 8,833 (53.3%). k=2.0: median 0, max 12, zero 50.4%, touches 13,874 (83.7%).
measured_not_estimated.verdict: k=1.0 PASSES comfortably -- median 0 <= 9, max 6 <= 19, zero-fraction 83.6% > 0. A 31x reduction at the maximum. RECORDED EXPLICITLY: the pre-declared PRIMARY passed, so NO re-selection occurred after seeing the figures. k=0.5 and k=2.0 remain what they were declared to be -- sensitivity checks, not promotion candidates.
measured_not_estimated.falsifiability_quantified: Unfiltered, 0.0% of bars have zero eligible levels -- price is LITERALLY always near a level, confirming Red Team's charge numerically. At k=1.0 it is 83.6%: on five bars in six NO level is in play, so the claim 'price reacts to a level' can now FAIL. Saturation resolved, measured.
measured_not_estimated.filter_does_not_destroy_the_population: 53.3% of touches are RETAINED at k=1.0 despite the 31x density cut. Structural rather than lucky: a level about to be touched is BY CONSTRUCTION already near price, so it passes the filter exactly when it matters -- what gets removed is the distant levels that were never going to be touched, which IS the dilution. Now measured rather than assumed.

primitive_b_density_filter_v2_7_41.what_the_filter_does_NOT_fix: 8,833 retained touches is the SAME ORDER OF MAGNITUDE as the three cited failures (DZ x FVG 18,275 trades / -$2,432; CAND-0020 34,006 / -15,409 R; CAND-0024 18,852 / -2,605 R). The filter resolves SATURATION and FALSIFIABILITY -- the two things Red Team demanded -- but NOT VOLUME. A candidate built on filtered B remains exposed to the too-many-zones pattern and must add its OWN selectivity. MANDATORY: any candidate on B reports its final trigger count BEFORE reporting any performance figure, since all three failures were discovered only after the volume had already been generated.

two_prohibitions_honoured.compensates_nothing: The filter is strictly a density reduction on the distance axis. D2 (equal highs/lows produce no swing) remains exactly what it is -- a permanent interpretive restriction, neither compensated nor circumvented here. D7, F4 and the D3_bis block boundaries are untouched.
two_prohibitions_honoured.threshold_not_chosen_after_results: k and the effectiveness threshold were fixed before measurement, the threshold deriving from the already-published 89/188 baseline rather than from the outcome. DECISIVE SAFEGUARD: the density measurement is P&L-BLIND -- it contains only level counts and touch counts, no performance figure whatsoever. Calibrating a filter on DENSITY is its declared purpose; calibrating on RESULTS would have been the abuse to avoid. The measurement cannot become a tuning backdoor because it contains no performance number to tune against.

prediction_test_CLOSED_missing_point_mea.the_invariant: Geometric touch rates: 47.7% / 47.3% / 48.1% -- a 0.8-point range across a ~35x period ratio. Scale-invariant. element_1_direction_test.requirement_transfers_construction_does_: At CAND-0028 (Mid) both arms have targets: the two session extremes. At CAND-0006 a WEEKLY_HIGH fade arm has a target (WEEKLY_LOW) but the inverse arm has NONE -- no weekly level exists ABOVE the weekly high. Keeping the target would make the arms differ in EXIT MECHANISM as well as direction, so a difference could not be attributed to direction.
element_1_direction_test.matched_pair_specified: Same touch bars, same entry. d = |entry - touch-bar extreme on the fade side| = CAND-0006s own declared stop distance, floored by min_executable_risk. Arm F: declared direction, stop = entry -/+ d. Arm I: opposite direction, stop = entry +/- d, THE SAME d mirrored. BOTH arms exit on the week-boundary time-stop ONLY. H0: mean(net_R|F) <= mean(net_R|I), paired on the same event, block bootstrap (L>=28) applied to the DIFFERENCE. The only symmetric option that invents no parameter.
element_1_direction_test.non_degeneracy_verified: With shared d and shared time-stop the arms are NOT mirror images, because the STOP breaks the symmetry: if F is stopped at -1R, I keeps running to the week boundary. That asymmetry is exactly where a direction advantage would manifest.
element_1_direction_test.amplifier_quantified: At weekly scale only 2.2% of touches have the markets own bias on the fade side, so CAND-0006 is COUNTER-BIAS in 97.8% of cases BY CONSTRUCTION (daily 73.5%, session 66.4%). The arms are therefore ASYMMETRICALLY informative: an F win is STRONG (it beats an arm that is trend-aligned almost always), while an I win is CONFOUNDED with plain trend-following and must additionally beat a bias-matched null on bars with NO level.
element_1_direction_test.four_outcomes_pre_committed: (1) F>I significant -> fade transfers to weekly. (2) I>F AND I beats the bias-matched null -> CAND-0006 REJECTED as framed; this does NOT promote a continuation thesis, which is a NEW hypothesis chosen AFTER the result and therefore requires its own family slot AND untouched data (sealed holdout or fresh). (3) I>F but does NOT beat the bias-matched null -> trend-following, not the level; rejected, nothing new. (4) Neither significant -> level inert at weekly; archived.
element_1_direction_test.why_outcome_2_is_the_load_bearing_guard: Without it every outcome is explicable: fade wins -> grammar confirmed; inverse wins -> the amplifier explains it so continuation was the real thesis. Both outcomes explained = unfalsifiable test. Closed in advance, not afterwards.
element_1_direction_test.decision_rule_conjunctive: The policy passes only if it beats zero AND F beats I. A fade that beats its inverse but loses money is not tradeable; a profitable policy whose direction rule is no better than its own inverse has not shown the level matters.

cand0006_protocol_and_backlog_v2_7_43.element_2_complete_only_conditioning: Red Team is directionally right and quantitatively wrong. The conditioning is real, in the predicted direction, and negligible in magnitude. Declared WITH the figure rather than as an open-ended warning; a CAND-0006 result reads as valid for complete weeks, which are 94% of the population.

element_3_fdr_family_sub_grouping_REJECT.decision: NO. The {CAND-0001, CAND-0027, CAND-0006} level-fade sub-family is refused.
element_3_fdr_family_sub_grouping_REJECT.derived_reason: A sub-family of three applies alpha over 3 instead of alpha over 7+K, LOOSENING the correction precisely for the three most favoured candidates. element_3_fdr_family_sub_grouping_REJECT.observation_re_homed_not_discarded: It belongs in two other places: DEPENDENCE (shared grammar across periods = POSITIVE dependence, PRDS-compatible, BH stays valid) and ANALYSIS (the three ARE the period gradient measured above, reported side by side). An ANALYSIS grouping, never an alpha partition -- the same separation as the family versus exploration ledgers.

element_4_S2_threshold.meaning_preserved_unlike_CAND_0003: The stop is beyond the level; widened by the floor it remains beyond the level. At CAND-0003 the floor VOIDED the stops structural meaning because the stop WAS the inversion boundary. Not so here.
element_4_S2_threshold.RR_protected_by_a_distant_target: The target is a full weekly range away, so R:R stays large even when floored. S2 bites on FREQUENCY, not on quality -- the opposite of CAND-0003 and for a different reason than CAND-0007.
element_4_S2_threshold.cannot_bias_the_direction_test: d is SHARED across both arms, so the floor applies identically to each and cannot tilt the comparison. A property of the construction, not an assumption.

element_5_not_a_subset_but_not_independe.measured: Weekly touches (COMPLETE) = 258. Also a daily PDH/PDL touch on the SAME bar = 105 (40.7%). Implied fade direction AGREES in 105 (100% of overlaps); OPPOSES in 0 (0.0%).
element_5_not_a_subset_but_not_independe.consequence: Positive dependence, PRDS-compatible, BH remains valid, NO partition needed. Overlap fraction reported per regime before any test, exactly as required for the CAND-0009 pair.
element_5_not_a_subset_but_not_independe.retroactive_clarification: This settles what the CAND-0009 problem actually was: not subset status, but the SIGN. family_and_exploration_counts.family: 7 (locked, monotone) + new category-C not yet included: 0012, 0017, 0019, 0026, 0027, 0028, 0029, 0030, 0031 = +9 => 16 now; up to 22 if CAND-0006 and all five Primitive-B candidates pass triage.

family_and_exploration_counts.BH_is_not_Bonferroni: alpha/m is the threshold ONLY for the smallest p-value. Under BH the k-th ordered p-value faces k*alpha/m. At m=16, alpha=0.05: p(1)<=0.0031, p(5)<=0.0156, p(8)<=0.0250, p(16)<=0.05. Family growth costs far less than the Bonferroni intuition suggests, and multiple genuine effects protect each other. This dissolves part of the anxiety driving the archive-to-preserve-power instinct -- correct archiving remains justified because negatives do not deserve testing, NOT because the family is dangerous.

the_six_are_not_one_group.CAND_0023_is_a_different_case_entirely: n=7 -- FOUR TIMES BELOW the N_MIN=25 reporting floor. NOT 'decisively negative' but UNTESTED: -1.9 R over 7 trades is noise. triage_criterion_three_outcomes.A_ARCHIVE_NEGATIVE: n >= N_MIN in every regime AND negative expectancy in ALL regimes AND no positive year. Does NOT consume family.
triage_criterion_three_outcomes.B_ARCHIVE_INSUFFICIENT: n < N_MIN in any regime -- the candidate was NEVER testable. NOT negative evidence. Requires funnel decomposition before any conclusion. Does NOT consume family.
triage_criterion_three_outcomes.C_FORMAL_PROTOCOL: Anything else -- mixed sign, marginal, or positive somewhere. Consumes one family slot.

If evidence changes -- a material cost correction, or a re-framing as CAND-0006 received -- an archived candidate may return, AND CONSUMES A SLOT AT THAT POINT. Not a free door.

family_governance_two_ledgers.the_distinction: FAMILY LEDGER (sets alpha) = how many hypotheses were FORMALLY TESTED, meaning a p-value and a verdict. EXPLORATION LEDGER (for honest reporting) = how many candidates were LOOKED AT, regardless of outcome. Two numbers, two purposes, must not be conflated.
family_governance_two_ledgers.why_archiving_negatives_does_not_violate: FDR control protects against FALSE POSITIVES -- it governs the fraction of REJECTIONS that are false. A candidate never tested produces no rejection; a decisively-negative archived candidate produces no rejection either. Therefore archiving negatives CANNOT inflate FDR. This is not a loophole but a consequence of what FDR actually measures.
family_governance_two_ledgers.what_archiving_WOULD_bias_if_undeclared: The apparent HIT RATE. 'We tested 7 and 3 worked' would be badly misleading if 19 were examined. Hence the exploration ledger must be kept VISIBLE even though it never enters alpha. This resolves the mandate's tension: there was never a need to choose between testing everything (destroying power) and archiving silently (hiding exploration).
family_governance_two_ledgers.rule_fixed_now: FAMILY = 7 + K, where K = candidates that PASS TRIAGE and are formally tested. MK batch contributes K += 0. Session batch contributes K += however many reach category C AFTER screening. EXPLORATION = 7 + 12 + everything subsequent, reported alongside any result. The criterion is fixed BEFORE the session screening completes, so it cannot be adjusted on results -- the same pattern as the V1/V2/V3 family rule (2+K fixed before any count existed).
family_governance_two_ledgers.dependence_verified: 0026 is a subset of 0027; 0029/0030/0031 are subsets of 0027 plus a second structure -- SUBSET relations, hence POSITIVE dependence, PRDS-compatible, so BH remains valid. Unlike the CAND-0001/CAND-0009 pair, the family's only negative dependence, already resolved by partition at v2.7.35.

session_batch_protocols_conditional_on_t.shared: Reused unchanged from STAT-BATCH-A-0001/A-0002: the 3 regimes; N_MIN=25 suppress-not-flag; WP-5' block_bootstrap (L>=28) on net_R; BH-FDR alpha=0.05 over the family of 7+K; sealed holdout; 2-fold expanding-window walk-forward on the established regime boundaries.
session_batch_protocols_conditional_on_t.W_incr_mandatory_for_four: 0026 (subset of 0027) and 0029/0030/0031 (subsets of 0027 plus a second structure): H0 = mean(net_R_subset) <= mean(net_R_0027 | THE SAME bars), computed on the exact subset where the narrower candidate fires -- never on the parent's larger population, never against a random null. Identical to CAND-0007 and CAND-0010.
session_batch_protocols_conditional_on_t.CAND_0028_approach_side_is_a_hypothesis_: session_levels.py established that Mid has NO intrinsic side and that any policy must DECLARE how direction is determined. Alpha declared 'approach side' -- but declaring an assumption does not validate it, and here the assumption carries the ENTIRE trade direction. The correct null is NOT zero but the REVERSED rule: H0 = mean(net_R | approach side) <= mean(net_R | REVERSED side), on THE SAME touch bars. Reason: a positive result against zero could stem entirely from Mid touches having an edge in SOME direction, with the approach-side rule contributing nothing. Only comparison against the reversed rule isolates the assumption's contribution -- the same incremental logic as W-incr, applied to a DIRECTION rule rather than a filter.
session_batch_protocols_conditional_on_t.feed_alignment_is_a_DEMO_precondition: 'Asia High in backtest is not Asia High live' is a BACKTEST-TO-LIVE TRANSFER problem, not a backtest-validity problem. It does NOT affect the statistical protocol, which runs on discovery data. It becomes a MANDATORY precondition before any of the six reaches DEMO: the live-computed session level must be verified to match the backtest-computed one. Same category as 'cost is OBSERVED, not modeled' -- a transfer gap routed to the stage where it matters.

triage_criterion_and_batch_protocols_v2_.F4_alarm_measured_at_zero: Verified directly in phase1_screening_results.json: ambiguous_dual_sign_choch_bars_per_regime = {bear: 0, bull: 0, correction: 0}, total 0. triage_criterion_and_batch_protocols_v2_.weekly_prediction_metric_fixed_before_re: Five of the six session candidates inherit the 'level reached by rallying up, traded short' structure; only 0028, via containment, is exempt. The v2.7.40 prediction was that the anti-correlation worsens with period length, so SESSION should suffer LESS than DAILY. METRIC: the bias-aligned fraction of touches. MEASURED: weekly = 2.2% (6/275). REQUIRED: the DAILY (PDH/PDL) fraction computed in the SAME pass, so the comparison is like-for-like rather than across different metrics. CONFIRMS: ordering session > daily > weekly. REFUTES: session <= daily, in which case the prediction is wrong and is to be recorded as such. Fixed before results, with the refutation condition written explicitly.

Nothing runs before (1). boundary_convention.rule: All epoch ranges in this manifest (discovery_range, intra_segment_embargo, sealed_range, and any other {start_epoch, end_epoch} pair) are HALF-OPEN: a bar at epoch t belongs to the range iff start_epoch <= t < end_epoch.
boundary_convention.verification: Directly recomputed bar counts for all three M15_v2 regime discovery blocks from data/market/OANDA_XAUUSD_M15.csv using the manifest's own discovery_range epochs. Half-open gives bear=52,403 / bull=52,851 / correction=25,237, exactly matching Research Lab's already-published, invariant-checked figures (sum 130,491). Closed-both-ends gives bear=52,404 (matching VE's independent count) with bull/correction unchanged -- confirming the recurring one-bar discrepancies (VE vs Research Lab on this block; historically Set A 67,321 vs 67,322 and Set B 16,830 vs 16,831) are half-open-vs-closed ambiguity, not a data error.
boundary_convention.why_half_open_is_correct: Adjacent sub-ranges within a segment (discovery_range -> intra_segment_embargo -> sealed_range) share boundary epochs. Only half-open partitions them cleanly, with no bar double-counted at a shared boundary and no gap.
boundary_convention.shared_function_contract: Specified for edge_research/split_manifest.py (the shared reader module; Statistician does not own this file and does not implement it there): def in_range(epoch: int, range_dict: dict) -> bool: return range_dict['start_epoch'] <= epoch < range_dict['end_epoch']. Every division counting bars within a manifest range calls this rather than reimplementing the inequality -- the convention is declared once, mechanically, and is not to be recalculated or re-litigated per discrepancy.
boundary_convention.not_retroactively_resolved: Set A (67,321 vs 67,322) and Set B (16,830 vs 16,831) are from an earlier pipeline already closed through discussion at the time; not reopened. This rule governs all ranges in this manifest going forward.

cross_verification_spec_scope_ruling.question: Does CROSS_VERIFICATION_SPEC (containment / aggregation correspondence / non-overlap / negative completeness / absence of orphans) apply to verification/measurement CODE, or only to derived DATA artifacts? Concrete tension: under Path A, Validation Engine both writes the tests and runs the Step 2 volume-audit measurement on its own test/measurement code, with no independent third-party check of that code.
cross_verification_spec_scope_ruling.ruling: CROSS_VERIFICATION_SPEC applies to derived DATA ARTIFACTS at risk of silent sealed-data leakage via incorrect manifest-boundary construction (its five properties are all about verifying an HTF-resampled bar against the manifest's discovery-block boundaries). It does NOT generically apply to verification/measurement code that only reads through an already-established, mechanically-safe discovery_range mask -- such code cannot leak sealed data by construction, regardless of who wrote it. VE's Step 1 (independent test-writing against Architect's/CEO's modules) and Step 2 (volume-audit measurement, confirmed to read only through the manifest's own discovery mask) do not trigger the spec; no third-party formal re-run of the five properties is required.
cross_verification_spec_scope_ruling.explicit_limit: This ruling does not extend to code in general. If VE's test/measurement code is ever reused as a PERSISTENT artifact that other divisions rely on for OTHER hypotheses (not this one-time D3 diagnostic), the calculus changes -- a repeatedly-relied-upon verification tool warrants independent review even though it is not itself an HTF-resampled data artifact. Written explicitly so this scope is not reinterpreted or widened later without re-deciding it.
cross_verification_spec_scope_ruling.f1_absolute_import_confirmed: Separately confirmed (not by analogy): liquidity_mechanics.py's absolute import of market_structure is consistent with code/'s actual convention -- code/ has no __init__.py and all of its modules (including mstrat.py's 'from alpha_lab import CFG') import absolutely. Statistician's earlier premise ('the rest of the repo uses packages + relative imports') held only for validation_engine/ve/, not for code/. VE's finding stands as correctly nuanced.

displacement_filter.status: RE-DERIVED AND RATIFIED (Mandate 3.23) -- superseded the REOPENED state from v2.7.8. NEW filter is authoritative unconditionally -- see FINAL_VERDICT_RECLASSIFIED_v2_7_9 for why the resulting dilution (more small-displacement events now eligible) is an expected mechanical consequence of the lower floor, not an error.
displacement_filter.rule: EXCLUDE trades with displacement < 10.1 pips (R < $1.21). A filter on ELIGIBILITY, not a floor on RISK -- never touches R of a trade that passes it.
displacement_filter.derivation: Derived, NOT chosen from the reference points offered (18.0/14.0/10.1 pips at 20%/25%/33% cost/R): the threshold is the displacement at which the lab's ALREADY-EXISTING 3x cost-stress convention (code/alpha_lab.py:197, c2: spread_ticks*=3, slip_ticks*=3 -> cost_stress=3*0.40=1.20, already used for sensitivity testing per STATISTICIAN_NET_OF_COST_OUTCOME_DEFINITION_v1.0.md SS5) would consume the ENTIRE risk of the trade (cost_stress/R=100%): (displacement+2)*0.10=1.20 -> displacement=10.0 pips (10.1 on discrete data). At 1x/default cost this is cost/R=33.1% -- coincides with the loosest of the three reference points, not because it was picked among them, but because that IS where the existing stress convention saturates.

Any mapping produced now cannot be shown independent of the result -- disclosed explicitly, same category as prior self-caught ordering issues (ratifying unread code, the 8->6 count correction), per Statistician's own standing discipline.
bootstrap_method.why_no_mapping_was_produced: Beyond the ordering problem: a density->phi mapping onto this AR(1) curve is not just untimely, it targets the WRONG INSTRUMENT. The classical overlapping-window autocorrelation formula (rho_1=(k-m)/k, k=20-bar horizon, m=6.2-bar average spacing =~69%) describes a FINITE-MEMORY process -- autocorrelation hits exactly zero beyond lag~20. AR(1)'s phi describes INFINITE geometric decay. Matching only the lag-1 correlation ignores exactly the property that matters for a block bootstrap with L=28: a 28-bar block fully CONTAINS a 20-bar-wide true dependency window, something no finite block length achieves against a true AR(1) (which never fully decays). A lag-1-matched phi could overstate OR understate the real risk -- the AR(1) curve answers a different question than the one LM-001's actual overlap mechanism poses. This is why the resolution is a new, purpose-built calibration (WP-5'), not a mapping onto the existing curve.

SMC_S2.mechanics: BOS at bar b in direction D (close beyond a CLASSIFIED swing) -> a CHoCH (opposite structural break) occurs within <=20 bars (group A, reused as the qualification window) -> entry at next-open after the CHoCH bar, direction = OPPOSITE of the original BOS (fade). No CHoCH in window -> event not eligible (excluded, not a separate failure outcome).
SMC_S2.threshold: spike = distance from entry to the broken BOS-level extremum + 2 pips.
SMC_S2.population: BOS events on M15_v2 discovery bars followed by a qualifying within-window CHoCH, minus the [10.1,65.0) filter.
SMC_S2.horizon_group: A (both the CHoCH-qualification window and the net_R measurement window)

primitives: D6 wick/close asymmetry re-applied to the BOS level itself
SMC_S3.mechanics: BOS at bar b in direction D -> a later bar's WICK touches the broken level within <=20 bars but its CLOSE stays on the breakout side (does not close back through) -> entry at next-open, direction = SAME as BOS (continuation). Mechanically distinct from SMC_S2 on the same retest bar (a bar cannot simultaneously close-through and not-close-through), though both can originate from the same BOS.
SMC_S3.threshold: spike = distance from entry to the retested level + 2 pips.

primitives: market_structure (>=2 consecutive same-direction CLASSIFIED swings, e.g. HH+HL or LH+LL)
SMC_S7.mechanics: Once a trend is established (>=2 consecutive same-direction swings), the NEXT swing continues it (a new HL higher / LH lower, no CHoCH triggered) -> entry at next-open after that swing's confirmed_idx, direction = the established trend.
SMC_S7.threshold: spike = distance from entry to the new swing extreme + 2 pips.
SMC_S7.horizon_group: A (default, no family-specific derivation given -- declared as such, not hidden)

definition_2_OrderBlock_Breaker.status: RATIFIED WITH TWO FIXES, specified before any implementation
definition_2_OrderBlock_Breaker.problem_1_zone_contradiction_fixed: For a bearish OB, body=[Close,Open] (Open>Close). The proposed formula [Open,Low] covers body PLUS the lower wick, a materially larger zone than 'the body' the text claims. DECIDED: active zone = the BODY, [Close_Bdown,Open_Bdown] -- the text's stated intent is correct, the formula is the error, formula corrected not the concept. Reasoning: the wick already has an established, exclusive role in this lab (D6: wick=penetration/touch, close=confirmation) -- including the wick in the OB zone itself would make 'touching the OB' ambiguous (wick-touch vs body-touch would mean different things), breaking the discipline already applied at MK-03 Q4/Q6.
definition_2_OrderBlock_Breaker.problem_2_E010_circularity_preempted: E010 failed because its selection window ('OB not yet violated within the test horizon') and measurement window ('did price continue within the SAME horizon') were IDENTICAL (min(idx+1+480,n) both places). Specified now, before VE implements, to prevent the same defect: (1) VALIDITY window -- an OB stays active from formation until EITHER (a) a wick touch in the zone (D7-analog consumption, used once, no re-arm) OR (b) a decisive CLOSE beyond the zone (becomes a 'breaker' -- reused verbatim from the already-ratified E010/E012 inversion criterion, Mandate 3.14). (a) and (b) are DIFFERENT events; (a) does not imply (b). (2) MEASUREMENT window -- begins ONLY at the qualifying event bar (a) or (b), never at OB formation, running the group-A horizon (20 bars) forward from THAT point. By construction these two windows cannot collapse into the same window computed twice, unlike E010's identical selection/measurement windows.
definition_2_OrderBlock_Breaker.implementation_status: IMPLEMENTED (code/order_block_void.py, commit edca965) -- zone + window separation frozen exactly as specified above. OB formation criterion (which candle becomes an OB) was NotImplementedError -- RATIFIED at Mandate 3.22, see order_block_formation_criterion_v2_7_8 (top-level) for the specification (E010 displacement/expansion qualifier + body-engulfment of the prior opposite candle's body, no volume filter). Still not implemented in code as of this manifest version; VE implements per the ratified spec.

cost_constant_correction_v2_7_8.source: CEO Mandate 3.22 -- CEO independently verified in code/mstrat.py that TICK=0.10 is wrong for XAUUSD (quoted to 2 decimals -> TICK=0.01), a 10x error inherited via copy-paste into code/alpha_lab.py and code/lm001_geometry_audit.py, and used in TWO distinct roles: (a) converting spread/slip tick-counts to a dollar cost, (b) converting raw dollar distances to 'pips' throughout the LM-001/SMC pipeline.
cost_constant_correction_v2_7_8.verification: Statistician independently confirmed code/mstrat.py:10 (TICK=0.1), :45 (cost=(spread_ticks+slip_ticks)*TICK), :53 (min_exec=max(2*spread_ticks*TICK,5*TICK,0.10*atr)), AND, going one line further than the order's own citation, :63 (Rs.append((dirn*(ex-entry)-2*cost)/risk)) -- the round-trip deduction is 2*cost, not cost. This resolves an internal ambiguity in Statistician's own prior citations of this formula, and catches a small slip in the order's own arithmetic (its written '(spread_ticks+slip_ticks)*TICK=2x0.1=0.40' literally equals 0.20, not 0.40 -- the true 0.40 only emerges via the code's separate 2*cost multiplier, which the order's walkthrough did not unpack).

TICK_corrected.source: Instrument spec verified via CEO's real account (Fusion Markets Classic): XAUUSD quoted to 2 decimals (e.g. 4033.84/4033.89), confirmed at the SOURCE (the account), not the code that copies the constant.

cost_round_trip_corrected.derivation: Real account: zero commission per lot, typical spread 5-15 ticks (at corrected TICK, $0.05-$0.15). Uses the MIDPOINT of the stated range (10 ticks, $0.10 full spread), not the single tightest observed example ($0.05) -- conservative-when-uncertain, the same convention applied throughout this lab. Slippage = spread (CEO's stated convention) -> spread_ticks=slip_ticks=5 (half of the 10-tick full spread each, preserving the code's existing per-side structure). cost_round_trip = 2*(5+5)*0.01 = $0.20. slip_ticks=1 does NOT survive at the corrected scale (would represent $0.01 of slip, unrealistically tight for a real OTC/CFD account) -- corrected to 5.

cost_constant_correction_v2_7_8.why_R_does_not_10x: Verified algebraically, not assumed: R_dollars=(displacement_pips+2)*TICK=(distance_dollars/TICK+2)*TICK=distance_dollars+2*TICK. The raw geometric distance term is TICK-INVARIANT; only the small '+2 pip buffer' term scales with TICK (0.20->0.02, a $0.18 shift per trade, not a 10x blowup). Self-corrected during this mandate after an initial miscalculation suggested a near-degenerate eligible band -- resolved via this exact algebra.

order_block_formation_criterion_v2_7_8.rule: A candle forms an Order Block iff: (a) it qualifies as an 'impulse' candle by the already-ratified E010 displacement/expansion criterion (range[i]>1.5*ATR14[i-1] AND |close[i]-open[i]|>=0.5*range[i], Mandate 3.21) -- reused verbatim, not re-derived; AND (b) its body [min(O,C),max(O,C)] fully engulfs the body of the immediately preceding OPPOSITE-direction candle. No volume filter (consistent with the volume-filter-elimination already ratified for the core OB primitive, Mandate 3.21). The OB's zone/anchor is the ENGULFED candle's own body (unchanged from Mandate 3.20), not the impulse candle's body.
order_block_formation_criterion_v2_7_8.not_a_contradiction_with_IFVG: The order flagged apparent tension with IFVG's inversion rule ('NOT single-bar body-engulfment'). Not a contradiction: IFVG answers WHEN an already-existing zone INVERTS (can be many bars after formation, first qualifying close beyond the zone); this criterion answers WHICH candle BECOMES a zone in the first place (a single-bar formation event, by construction). Different questions, legitimately different answers.

demandzone_primitive_v2_7_8.status: RATIFIED, new primitive, distinct from OrderBlock
demandzone_primitive_v2_7_8.boundaries: [High,Low] (full candle range, wick included) -- NOT [Close,Open]. Derived from the CEO's own stated subset relationship: OrderBlock's body [Close,Open] is ALWAYS a geometric subset of [High,Low] for any candle by construction; the subset relation only holds if DemandZone=[High,Low] (if DemandZone were also [Close,Open] it would be identical to OrderBlock, not a distinct macro concept).
demandzone_primitive_v2_7_8.consumption: DemandZone does NOT consume -- persistent, re-testable repeatedly (CEO's explicit framing). The nested OrderBlock DOES consume via D7 (unchanged). Two different lifecycle rules on nested-but-semantically-distinct objects -- intentional design, not an inconsistency: DemandZone is the macro/persistent reference (like a classical S/R level); OrderBlock is the narrower, single-use claim ('this exact body, as impulse origin, valid once').
demandzone_primitive_v2_7_8.intersection_mechanical: Entry condition: price in [DemandZone_low, DemandZone_high] for a formation event A, AND price in [OB_close,OB_open] for an unmitigated OrderBlock from a formation event B. TRIVIAL reading (A=B, same candle): always true by the subset relation, adds no information beyond the OB alone. SUBSTANTIVE reading (A != B, a DIFFERENT/older DemandZone geometrically overlapping a DIFFERENT, still-unmitigated OrderBlock): the reading that gives 'intersection' genuine meaning. RECOMMENDED: the substantive (A!=B) reading -- flagged explicitly for CEO/VE confirmation before implementation, not assumed.
demandzone_primitive_v2_7_8.anti_E010_window_separation: Extended to the compound object: DemandZone's validity = active for its entire containing block (D4), never expires early (non-consuming). Measurement window begins ONLY at the COMPOUND entry event (price inside an active DemandZone AND inside an unmitigated OB simultaneously), never at either primitive's own formation bar.

weighted_RR_CORRECTED.status: CORRECTION to the order's own arithmetic, verified not just confirmed
weighted_RR_CORRECTED.order_stated: 0.75x1.4R + 0.25x2.1R = 1.575 approx 1.58R -- treats 1.4 and 2.1 directly as R-multiples.
weighted_RR_CORRECTED.error: R = SL = 0.7xATR, NOT 1xATR. In true R-units: TP1 = 1.4xATR/0.7xATR = 2.0R (not 1.4R); TP2 = 2.1/0.7 = 3.0R (not 2.1R). The order's own figures are ATR-multiples, not R-multiples -- conflating the two understates the real payoff.
weighted_RR_CORRECTED.corrected: 0.75x2.0R + 0.25x3.0R = 2.25R (not 1.58R) -- a favorable correction, real profit potential is larger than the order's own estimate.
weighted_RR_CORRECTED.required_winrate_formula: w* = (1+cost/R)/(RR_eff+1) = (1+cost/R)/3.25 -- NOT a single number, R=0.7xATR varies with current ATR (same lesson as Mandate 3.13's R-heterogeneity finding, re-applies identically here).
weighted_RR_CORRECTED.required_winrate_range_v2_7_10: At cost/R->0 (large ATR), w*->1/3.25=30.77% approx 31% (CEO's cited figure -- the zero-cost limit, not the real value at any finite R). eligibility_filter.sufficiency_decision_v2_7_10: RATIFIED (Mandate 3.24): the ATR floor ALONE is sufficient -- no ceiling added. Here R=0.7*ATR is PROPORTIONAL to current volatility by construction -- an extreme-ATR bar does not produce a disproportionately risky R in normalized terms, R simply scales with it. oracle_domain_question_UNRESOLVED_not_ve.likely_direction: A null calibrated on longer-than-real dependency generally produces MORE resampling variance than warranted -- making the test MORE conservative (harder to reject H0 in either direction), not less. If so, true p-values under a correctly-recalibrated null (matched to the realized ~1-2 bar dependency) would likely be SMALLER than reported, not larger -- most relevant to the correction regime (p=0.186, the least overwhelming non-rejection).
oracle_domain_question_UNRESOLVED_not_ve.standing_asymmetric_rule_applied: Same rule as LM-001 (Mandate 3.22): negative/null results (bear, bull) are robust to this uncertainty (a possibly-too-conservative null works in the safe direction for a negative conclusion). Does not change TODAY's verdict: none of the 3 p-values approach any plausible rejection threshold (~0.05) regardless.

new_oracle_domain_question_ANSWERED.question: Is block_bootstrap@v1 (validated for a single overlapping-window net_R series) the right tool for an A-vs-C comparison?
new_oracle_domain_question_ANSWERED.answer: NO, not directly -- A-vs-C is a matched 1:1 PAIRED comparison (each zone trigger matched to exactly one pullback-control partner by construction), a different statistical object than a one-sample overlapping-net_R mean test. The correct question is on the per-pair difference d_i = MFE_A_i - MFE_C_i, not on the two distributions separately -- a paired test (Wilcoxon signed-rank, or bootstrap on the paired mean/median difference) is both more appropriate and more powerful, since it automatically controls for anything common to a matched pair.
new_oracle_domain_question_ANSWERED.residual_dependence_flagged: Nearby trigger events could still be correlated in time (shared market conditions), meaning the PAIRS themselves might not be independent draws -- an analogous, not identical, concern to net_R's overlap dependence. RECOMMENDS reusing the block_bootstrap RESAMPLING MECHANICS (not its net_R calibration) applied to the time-ordered d_i series, run ALONGSIDE a plain iid bootstrap as a baseline -- if the two agree closely the finding is robust to the dependence-calibration question; if they diverge, that divergence is itself the informative result (same category of reasoning as LM-001's own r_variance_note).
new_oracle_domain_question_ANSWERED.not_yet_run: This paired test has NOT been executed. Today's +28%/+38%/+46% pattern is an OBSERVATION, not a validated finding, per explicit instruction to say so plainly if that is the honest characterization. This diagnostic (like Measurement A' before it) does not consume the multiple-testing family -- it decides whether a real hypothesis is worth formulating, it is not the hypothesis test itself.
