obdz_atr_rescaling_inference_rejected_v2.verdict: NO -- not a valid independent justification. An impermissible inference, on three independent grounds, any one sufficient alone.
obdz_atr_rescaling_inference_rejected_v2.reason_1_no_edge_was_ever_established: H0 (mean(net_R)<=0) was not rejected in any regime (v2.7.24: p=0.637/0.861/0.288). The edge_brut figures being rescaled are unproven point estimates from a distribution the project's own test could not distinguish from zero. Multiplying an unproven estimate by an ATR ratio produces a larger unproven number, not new evidence of a real edge -- if the true population edge is zero or negative, no scale factor makes it positive, only larger in dollar terms while remaining zero or negative in the R-multiple terms that actually determine profitability.
obdz_atr_rescaling_inference_rejected_v2.reason_2_the_discovery_regimes_already_r: The argument silently assumes R-multiple edge is an ATR-invariant structural constant, with only cost's R-drag changing across volatility levels. The three discovery regimes contradict this directly: bull's R-multiple edge (-0.0776) is far MORE negative than bear's (-0.0134) despite bull having the LOWEST median ATR (1.27) of the three -- if edge were driven by ATR level, bull should look similar to the others once cost is accounted for; it does not. R-edge is regime-driven (bias, structure, participant behavior), not ATR-driven -- there is no single, portable R-edge value to transplant onto an unobserved present-day regime.
obdz_atr_rescaling_inference_rejected_v2.reason_3_extrapolation_far_outside_the_v: The proposed factor (3.4x-5.8x) extrapolates several times beyond the entire ATR range ever observed in the fitted data (1.27-2.19), onto a market that has structurally evolved for over a decade (liquidity, participant composition, algorithmic activity). The calculation additionally assumes the $0.20 cost figure stays flat as price and volatility rise 3-6x -- an assumption at least as likely wrong as right (spreads commonly widen in higher-volatility regimes) and unverifiable without new data. This is the same category of out-of-domain extrapolation this project has consistently declined elsewhere (the AR(1) oracle invalidated for scale, the wide-SL/TP diagnostic that degenerated into a drift measurement).
obdz_atr_rescaling_inference_rejected_v2.conditional_followup_declined: CTO's own conditional framing (if valid, the rejection is of the period not the strategy, and the next question is an ATR threshold derivable from fixed cost) is correctly structured logically, but the condition is not met -- reason 1 alone stops the chain, since deriving a threshold presupposes a real edge that was never established. S16_S17_NOT_TESTABLE.reason: block_bootstrap@v1 is validated STRICTLY for L>=H=20 (Mandate 3.20). S16 (H=92) and S17 (H=460) both ran at the SAME L=28 inherited mechanically from the Group-A Open-R contract -- at these horizons L=28<H, the exact condition (block shorter than the true dependency window) that invalidated the AR(1) regime at Mandate 3.17. block_bootstrap@v1 does not cover this configuration.
S16_S17_NOT_TESTABLE.consequence: Every p_wp5 reported for S16/S17 in this run is UNVALIDATED and UNUSABLE for any conclusion -- explicitly including S17's deceptively low figures (bear-new p=0.0265, correction-new p=0.0190). A low p-value from an uncalibrated estimator is not evidence; flagged as a trap, not a finding.
S16_S17_NOT_TESTABLE.additional_S17_correction_issue: n=27 at the old filter, below the nt>L=28 requirement -- p correctly returned None (a refusal to run underpowered, not a bug).
S16_S17_NOT_TESTABLE.recalibration_decision: NOT commissioned in this document -- a proper WP-5' recalibration at L>=92/L>=460 is a validation effort of similar scope to the original (new null generator sized to the true mechanism, dedicated FPR battery, pre-registered acceptance band), a new VE task, not a relabeling. S16/S17 remain NOT TESTABLE (oracle-uncalibrated) until such a recalibration is separately commissioned and executed.
